items.title: Sahara occidental : la dangereuse tentation marocaine
items.description: La volonté des autorités marocaines de prendre le contrôle des emprises de la MINURSO situées à l'est du mur de sable, notamment dans le secteur de Tifariti, marque un tournant dangereux dans le conflit au Sahara occidental . Après la liquidation du dispositif onusien, Rabat semble vouloir exploiter le vide sécuritaire pour étendre son contrôle aux territoires administrés par le Front Polisario. Sahara occidental : le Maroc joue avec le feu Une telle initiative exposerait le Maroc à une guerre asymétrique prolongée. Le Polisario dispose des moyens de mener des opérations de guérilla, de multiplier les attaques contre les positions militaires et les infrastructures économiques en territoire sahraoui occupé. Il pourrait ainsi imposer à l'armée marocaine une guerre d'usure. La pression militaire ne serait pas le seul front auquel Rabat devrait faire face. Dans les territoires sahraouis occupés, une nouvelle offensive marocaine raviverait la contestation politique et provoquerait des mouvements de révolte contre l'administration d’occupation marocaine. Mais le danger tient surtout à un possible élargissement régional du conflit. Toute progression militaire marocaine vers les territoires proches de la frontière sud-ouest de l'Algérie serait considérée comme une menace stratégique. Rabat commettrait une erreur fatale en croyant que la disparition de la MINURSO lui permet d'engager son armée au contact de la frontière algérienne. Dans le contexte de tensions bilatérales persistantes, un incident frontalier ou une escalade mal maîtrisée pourrait rapidement dégénérer en affrontement. Les conséquences dépasseraient alors largement le cadre du Sahara occidental. Le silence européen face à cette perspective est particulièrement préoccupant. Celui de l'Espagne l'est davantage encore. Ancienne puissance coloniale, elle demeure, au regard du droit international, la puissance administrante de jure du Sahara occidental. Madrid ne saurait donc se retrancher derrière son soutien politique au Maroc ni considérer que la disparition de la MINURSO met fin à ses responsabilités historiques et juridiques. Le silence incompréhensible de l’Espagne Cette attitude est d'autant plus incompréhensible que l'Espagne figure parmi les pays européens les plus exposés aux conséquences d'une reprise des hostilités. Une déstabilisation du Sahara occidental ne manquerait pas de provoquer de nouveaux mouvements migratoires vers les îles Canaries et les côtes espagnoles. Elle menacerait également les approvisionnements énergétiques, les intérêts économiques européens et les dispositifs de coopération sécuritaire avec les pays du Maghreb. Bruxelles semble faire preuve de la même indifférence. L'Union européenne dispose pourtant de moyens économiques, commerciaux et diplomatiques considérables pour dissuader Rabat de toute nouvelle aventure militaire. La France et l'Espagne, en raison de leur proximité avec les autorités marocaines, disposent d'une capacité d'influence particulière. Plutôt que de s'arroger un droit de regard totalement indu et scandaleux sur la coopération militaire entre l'Algérie et le Niger, cette Europe ferait mieux de regarder les menaces qui s'accumulent au Sahara occidental, au lieu de s'ériger en juge et de réclamer des comptes à des États souverains. En refusant de fixer des limites claires aux ambitions territoriales marocaines, les capitales européennes risquent de transformer leur soutien politique à Rabat en encouragement implicite à l'escalade. L'Europe pourrait alors payer le prix d'une politique de complaisance dont elle ne maîtrise ni les conséquences ni l'issue. Elle ne pourra pas prétendre avoir été prise au dépourvu si une nouvelle guerre au Sahara occidental débouche sur une confrontation de plus grande ampleur et une déstabilisation durable de toute la région. L’article Sahara occidental : la dangereuse tentation marocaine est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Festival du court métrage Ouaga Côté Court 2026 : 55 films de 33 pays au programme du 14 au 21 novembre
items.description: La 5e édition du Festival international du court métrage Ouaga Côté Court (OCC) se tiendra du 14 au 21 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, sous le thème « Le cinéma qui rassemble ». En prélude à l'événement, le comité d'organisation a animé une conférence de presse le samedi 7 novembre 2026 afin de présenter la programmation et les ambitions de cette édition. Du 14 au 21 novembre 2026, Ouagadougou accueille la 5e édition du Festival international du court métrage Ouaga Côté Court. 55 films de 33 pays sont inscrits au programme. Selon la promotrice du festival, Irène Tassembédo, l'initiative répond à un déficit structurel de diffusion des courts métrages sur le continent africain. « On produit des films, on forme de jeunes cinéastes, on développe des talents extraordinaires, mais où peut-on voir leurs œuvres ? Un film qui ne rencontre jamais son public, c'est une parole qui reste enfermée », a-t-elle déclaré. Pour elle, le cinéma doit constituer un espace de rencontre et de dialogue entre les peuples. « Je crois profondément que l'art doit circuler, qu'il doit provoquer des rencontres, ouvrir des fenêtres, bousculer nos certitudes et nous permettre de regarder l'autre autrement », a-t-elle ajouté, invitant les Ouagalais à se mobiliser pour ce rendez-vous cinématographique. Irène Tassembédo invitant les Ouagalais à se mobiliser du 14 au 21 novembre pour prendre part à ce rendez-vous cinématographique Le coordonnateur technique du festival, Jean-Baptiste Guiard-Schmid, a indiqué que 55 films issus de 33 pays avaient été retenus pour cette édition, répartis en 34 fictions, 11 documentaires et 10 films d'animation. Cette sélection résulte du travail d'un comité international composé de 32 membres, qui a examiné 736 productions provenant de 91 pays. Les projections se dérouleront chaque soir à partir de 18 heures au siège du FESPACO. Deux séances spéciales sont prévues le vendredi 20 novembre : la première, à 18 h 30, sera consacrée au jeune public, tandis que la seconde, à 20 h 15, mettra à l'honneur la création africaine. Au-delà des projections, plusieurs activités de formation et de rencontres professionnelles figurent au programme. Un atelier de renforcement des capacités en écriture de scénarios de courts métrages est prévu du 16 au 20 novembre, ainsi qu'un concours de pitch le 21 novembre 2026. Cette édition sera également marquée par la constitution d'un jury étudiant chargé de décerner un prix spécial lors de la cérémonie de clôture. Des concerts live seront organisés chaque soir en marge des projections, et 14 films seront récompensés au terme de la compétition. Le trophée qui sera remis lors de la clôture Parmi les œuvres sélectionnées figurent notamment « Je ne suis pas fou » de Kader Ouédraogo, « Amina Traoré, l'héritage du Mandé » de Kany Dembélé, « Forêt Blanche » de Thomas Grand et Joan Bastide , « The People's Blood » de Solo Ouédraogo et « The Kankurang » de Ciesay Imran. L'entrée aux projections est libre et gratuite . Plus de 5 000 spectateurs sont attendus autour du court métrage. Sidziguin Irène Corinne SAWADOGO Minute.bf

items.title: Troops rescue 119 civilians, recover eight vehicles in Borno
items.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have rescued 119 civilians abducted by terrorists and recovered eight vehicles during an operation in Borno. The military disclosed this in an operational report made available to Newsmen on Saturday in Abuja. The report said the operation was conducted by troops of 135 Special Forces Battalion while monitoring surveillance cameras along the Dutsen Kura-Bulazarma-Kamuya road. It said the troops sighted the terrorists abducting civilians and vehicles and mobilised through Mangari-Dora in Biu Local Government Area to foil the operation. According to the report, they engaged the terrorists, forcing them to abandon the abducted civilians and flee in disarray. It said the troops recovered eight vehicles and reunited the rescued civilians with their families. “They also discovered and detonated an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) around the Bam-Buratai Junction-Bulazarma general area. “In a separate development, a suspected fighter of Jama’atu Ahlis-Sunna Lidda’Awati Wal-Jihad (JAS) surrendered to troops of 202 Battalion at Ngurusoye Village, Bama Local Government Area. “The suspect reportedly fled his group’s enclave in Bula Daloye following clashes with the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and hardship. “He surrendered with an FN rifle and seven rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition and is currently in military custody for further action,” it said. The report said troops and members of the Hybrid Force arrested a suspected terrorist informant and collaborator at Ngamdu Town, Borno, on Nov. 5. It added that troops of Army Headquarters Garrison foiled an attempted abduction of a retired senior military officer and his son at Kurudu Phase Five, Abuja. According to the report, the assailants attacked the residence of the retired officer at about 4:05 a.m. on Saturday, adding that troops’ intervention forced the attackers to abandon their victims after inflicting knife wounds on their shoulders and heads. The report added that the injured victims were evacuated to a nearby hospital for medical attention. It said the troops of Operation Enduring Peace arrested two suspected burglars at Doi Community in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau on Saturday. The report said the suspects were allegedly attempting to break into a poultry house to steal chickens and were handed over to the police for further investigation. “In Benue, troops of Operation Whirl Stroke arrested a herder over alleged malicious grazing on farmland at Tse Tur, Gwer West Local Government Area. “The suspect was arrested at Umbago and remains in military custody for further action,” it said The post Troops rescue 119 civilians, recover eight vehicles in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: MLS: Messi remporte son deuxième Soulier d’or consécutif
items.description: Lionel Messi a décroché samedi son deuxième Soulier d’or consécutif de la MLS avec l’Inter Miami, à l’issue de la dernière journée de la saison régulière, au terme de laquelle le club floridien, champion en titre, a terminé 2è de la Conférence Est. Avec 26 buts inscrits, l’attaquant argentin devient le premier joueur de l’histoire du championnat nord-américain à remporter cette distinction deux saisons de suite. Il devance Petar Musa, du FC Dallas, qui a inscrit 22 buts. Muet lors du match nul (3-3) face à Charlotte, Messi s’est néanmoins illustré en délivrant deux passes décisives sur corner, contribuant ainsi à assurer à son équipe l’avantage du terrain pour les deux premiers tours des play-offs. Le club floridien termine la saison régulière avec 60 points, derrière Nashville, leader de la Conférence Est avec 77 points, un nouveau record. Il affrontera Columbus au premier tour des play-offs. items.description: The administrative setup in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans to establish faceless anti-terrorism courts in the province as part of its initiatives to strengthen the fight against terrorism, according to a briefing of the officials televised on Sunday. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi was also present at the briefing, where KP Secretary Home Amjad Ali Khan outlined several measures planned to step up the fight against terrorism and explained that witnesses in terrorism cases feared coming forward. “So, we have recently sent the amendment to set faceless anti-terrorism courts. items.title: Macron : un bunker secret pour fuir l’Élysée en cas de révolte
items.description: Le bunker serait situe hors de Paris. Pierre Gastineau, Antoine Izambard et Franck Renaud en parlent dans La Nouvelle Armee des ombres , leur livre paru le 28 octobre. Les trois journalistes, specialistes du renseignement, y retracent les discussions autour d'une eventuelle intrusion de manifestants a l'elysee et de la mise a l'abri d'Emmanuel Macron. Le quotidien britannique The Telegraph a repris leur enquete le 6 novembre. Ces projets auraient pris forme pendant les manifestations des Gilets jaunes, en 2018. Le 4 decembre 2018, au Puy-en-Velay, Emmanuel Macron avait ete pris a partie apres l'incendie de la prefecture. Ce deplacement aurait marque ses equipes de securite. Outre la protection des acces au palais, elles auraient envisage la possibilite de faire quitter Paris au president. Antoine Izambard a evoque cette periode sur France Inter le 6 novembre. Il a rappele : « Le pouvoir a tremble, tres clairement. » Les conseillers du president auraient alors examine plusieurs plans d'evacuation. Les emeutes de fevrier 1934, qui avaient entraîne la chute d'un gouvernement francais, auraient aussi ete evoquees lors de ces discussions. La presidentielle de 2027 sous surveillance Les services de securite envisageraient desormais plusieurs scenarios de crise apres la prochaine election presidentielle. Une victoire du Rassemblement national, parti de Marine Le Pen, pourrait provoquer, selon les hypotheses etudiees, une contestation des resultats dans la rue. Celle de Jean-Luc Melenchon, figure de La France insoumise, ferait redouter une resistance passive au sein de la police. D'apres les auteurs, le prefet de police de Paris, Patrice Faure, aurait reuni plusieurs fois ses equipes pour preparer une eventuelle insurrection. La police parisienne aurait aussi simule une journee sans telephones securises face a une cyberattaque majeure. Des militaires des forces speciales auraient etudie une intervention pour defendre le Parlement en cas de soulevement arme. Un pouvoir inquiet de la colere sociale Ces revelations surgissent au milieu des manifestations en France contre la vie chere . Le 7 novembre, l'intersyndicale de la jeunesse a recense 250 000 participants, contre 146 000 selon le ministere de l'Interieur. Des gaz lacrymogenes ont encore ete utilises dans plusieurs villes. Le livre revient egalement sur d'anciens fonds clandestins des services de renseignement, concus pour soutenir des reseaux de resistance en cas d'effondrement de l'etat. L'enquete met ainsi en lumiere des preparatifs qui depassent la protection personnelle du president Macron et portent sur la survie meme des institutions en cas de crise interieure.

items.title: Mahama earmarks GH¢10m for Media Development Fund in 2027 budget
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has announced a GH¢10 million allocation in the 2027 national budget to provide seed funding for the reactivated Media Development Fund. The funding is expected to support journalists’ welfare, professional training, investigative journalism, digital literacy and safety programmes within the media industry. Speaking at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards, President Mahama said the allocation followed his commitment at the previous year’s awards to revive the fund as part of efforts to strengthen the media landscape. He said the government would also partner with the GJA to attract contributions from private sector organisations and other corporate institutions to expand the fund’s resources. President Mahama disclosed that he intended to personally engage institutions, including KGL and the Bank of Ghana, to support the initiative. “I shall personally work with the GJA to get several other corporate institutions to contribute to the fund. So KGL, Bank of Ghana, all of you, we are coming to you to contribute to the Media Fund,” he said. He assured journalists that government would continue consultations with the GJA and other stakeholders to ensure the commitment translates into tangible assistance, while safeguarding the independence of the media. The President also called on senior journalists, particularly editors, to invest in mentoring young reporters by giving them opportunities to acquire practical newsroom experience. He said developing the next generation of journalists required more than formal training, stressing the importance of allowing young reporters to work alongside experienced editors and build specialised skills. “I encourage the association and experienced editors to make room for younger reporters to learn this work. A young journalist who can sit with an editor and work through a set of public accounts will carry that skill into every story that follows,” he said.

Ato Forson says New Economy will help Ghana attain an investment-grade rating
items.description: Ghana is seeking to secure an investment-grade credit rating through its New Economy programme, a move Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says will help reduce borrowing costs and improve access to long-term financing for local businesses. Speaking at a New Economy engagement in Accra, Dr Forson said the government was focused on strengthening the country’s economic fundamentals to restore investor confidence and improve Ghana’s standing in international financial markets. He recalled that Ghana’s domestic bond market suffered a major setback in 2022 following the country’s debt default and the implementation of the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP). According to the Finance Minister, the crisis disrupted access to credit lines for local banks and brought significant activity in the domestic bond market to a near standstill. Dr Forson said the government had since made progress in restoring confidence, with Ghana’s credit rating now at B. He noted, however, that the ultimate objective was to attain investment-grade status. “Now we have restored it, and the country is now rated B. We want to get to investment grade,” he said. An investment-grade rating would indicate a stronger assessment of Ghana’s ability to meet its debt obligations. It could also attract more institutional investors, including those whose investment mandates require securities to meet a minimum credit rating. Dr Forson said achieving this status could enable the government to secure financing at more favourable interest rates by widening the pool of investors willing to purchase its bonds. He also highlighted the potential benefits for the private sector, explaining that an improved sovereign credit rating could create more favourable financing conditions for Ghanaian businesses. In particular, he said a stronger credit profile could help establish a more vibrant corporate bond market, giving companies access to long-term capital beyond conventional bank loans. This would allow businesses to raise funds for expansion, acquire equipment, increase production capacity and undertake new investments. “If we are able to get to investment grade, we would have laid the foundation for corporate bonds and others to take off,” Dr Forson said. He stressed, however, that achieving the target would require sustained economic stability, predictable policies and a continued commitment to reforms. For the Finance Minister, securing an investment-grade rating is therefore not simply about improving Ghana’s credit standing, but also about creating a stronger financial environment in which the government and private businesses can access affordable, long-term funding.

Qui est Gadi Eisenkot, le faucon d’origine marocaine nommé Premier ministre d’Israël ?
items.description: Israël va-t-il tourner la page de Benyamin Netanyahu ? Le chef de l’opposition Gadi Eisenkot, d’origine marocaine, a été chargé par le président israélien Isaac Herzog de former un gouvernement. Ne disposant pas de la majorité absolue à l’issue des élections législatives de fin octobre, le nouveau Premier ministre a vingt jours pour trouver un accord avec d’autres formations politiques, notamment les partis arabes israéliens qui s'imposent comme l'arbitre de cette élection. Dans un contexte de normalisation et de rapprochement entre Tel-Aviv et Rabat, le gouvernement sortant de Benyamin Netanyahou comprend plusieurs ministres d'origine marocaine, mais c’est la première fois qu’un juif dont les parents sont originaires du Maroc atteint un tel poste de responsabilité en Israël. Gadi Eisenkot est né en 1960 à Tibériade, dans le nord d’Israël, d’un père et d’une mère originaires de Marrakech et de Casablanca respectivement. Militaire de carrière, il a été notamment chef d’état-major de l’armée israélienne entre 2015 et 2019. Gadi Eisenkot, loin d'être une colombe Bien qu'il s’oppose à Benyamin Netanyahou, Eisenkot n'est pas une colombe, comme le montrent ses états de service. Il a participé à de nombreuses guerres d’Israël contre les Palestiniens et les pays de la région, notamment à celles du Liban en 1982 et 2006 et à la dernière agression de Gaza en tant que ministre sans portefeuille et observateur dans le cabinet de guerre de Netanyahou. En tant que chef d'état-major, il est responsable de la répression de la « marche du retour » à Gaza qui a fait 200 morts et 18 000 blessés en 2018. Surtout, il est connu pour être le concepteur de la doctrine dite « Dahiya » qui préconise un usage disproportionné de la force, y compris contre les civils, lorsque l’armée israélienne est attaquée. C’est cette doctrine que Benyamin Netanyahou a appliquée après les attaques du 7 octobre 2023. items.title: Inuwa seeks common Northern policy framework to tackle out-of-school children
items.description: Advocates unified regional agenda, investment in agriculture, agro-allied industries to combat poverty, insecurity Sultan applauds Gombe governor’s Almajiri education reforms By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe Gombe State Governor and Chairman of the Northern States Governors’ Forum, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has called for a common policy framework and unified regional agenda to sustain education reforms, tackle the growing number of out-of-school children and accelerate human capital development across Northern Nigeria. The governor said addressing the region’s educational challenges required a coordinated approach that went beyond school enrolment to include poverty reduction, improved security, economic empowerment and the creation of sustainable livelihood opportunities for the growing population. Yahaya made the call at the 2026 Biennial Lecture and Awards Ceremony of the Barewa Old Boys Association (BOBA), held in Gombe, with the theme, “The Scourge of Out-of-School Children and the Implications for National Security.” Describing the theme as timely and critical to the future of Northern Nigeria, the governor warned that the increasing number of children outside the formal education system posed serious threats to social stability, economic productivity and national security. He observed that educational exclusion perpetuated poverty, widened inequality and exposed vulnerable children and young people to criminal exploitation, radicalisation and other antisocial tendencies. Yahaya recalled that when his administration assumed office in 2019, Gombe State had more than 500,000 out-of-school children, explaining that sustained interventions by his government had brought approximately 350,000 of them back into the classroom. He attributed the achievement to the declaration of a state of emergency in the education sector, construction of mega schools with expanded learning capacities, recruitment of more than 1,000 qualified teachers and establishment of Almajiri Integrated Learning Centres, among other initiatives. Drawing from the state’s experience, the governor urged Northern states to move away from fragmented interventions and embrace a common regional framework that would identify successful educational models, encourage their adoption across state boundaries and guarantee continuity. He proposed that the Northern States Governors’ Forum should provide the institutional platform for harmonising educational policies, coordinating priorities and strengthening collaboration among the 19 Northern states. According to him, a unified Northern Agenda would ensure that successful programmes initiated by successive administrations were sustained, while promoting the sharing of resources, expertise and best practices for regional development. He maintained that the magnitude of the challenges confronting Northern Nigeria required collective responsibility, stressing that no single state could effectively address the problem of out-of-school children in isolation. The governor also advocated the expansion and institutionalisation of student exchange programmes among Northern states to promote educational integration, cultural understanding and regional cohesion. He cited Gombe State’s experience of accommodating more than 800 students from outside the state as a model that could be replicated across the region through the establishment of special schools with expanded facilities. “If Gombe has the capacity to host more than 800 exchange students, I think it will be even better if we can have expanded schools in each of the 19 Northern states where we can accommodate a larger number. If Barewa can make this lot of impact, I would support having several Barewas across the North,” he said. Beyond education, Yahaya called for greater investment in agriculture, agro-allied industries, industrialisation and agricultural value chains, describing them as critical instruments for addressing poverty, unemployment and insecurity. He noted that Northern Nigeria possessed enormous agricultural potential which, if properly harnessed through modern farming techniques, processing facilities and value-chain development, could stimulate economic growth, create employment opportunities and improve household incomes. The governor explained that improving the economic circumstances of families would complement investments in education by enabling parents to support their children’s schooling and reducing the socioeconomic pressures that push vulnerable children into street activities and exploitation. He said his administration had continued to pursue an integrated development strategy in Gombe State, combining investments in education with infrastructure, agriculture and industrial development. Yahaya consequently challenged BOBA and other participants at the lecture to produce practical and implementable recommendations that would assist governments and stakeholders in addressing the out-of-school children crisis and the broader socioeconomic challenges facing the North. He assured that recommendations emerging from the engagement would be presented to the Northern States Governors’ Forum for consideration as part of efforts to strengthen a common regional approach to education and sustainable development. Earlier, the National President of BOBA, Major General Alwali Jauji Kazir, described the theme of the lecture as timely, noting that it reflected the association’s commitment to the educational welfare of Nigerian children. Kazir emphasised the importance of school safety, particularly in Northern Nigeria, and called for improved learning environments, adequate teaching resources and deliberate government policies to ensure that children were enrolled, retained and supported to complete their education. Similarly, the Chairman of the BOBA Board of Trustees, General Yakubu Gowon, said the challenge of out-of-school children could be addressed through deliberate policies and the provision of appropriate conditions and incentives to encourage school enrolment, retention and completion. His message was delivered by the Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, who appreciated the government and people of Gombe State for their hospitality and commended Governor Yahaya for his personal commitment and sacrifices towards the success of the 2026 Biennial Lecture. Speaking in his capacity as Deputy Chairman of the BOBA Board of Trustees, the Sultan described education as a fundamental pillar of Islam, which encourages the pursuit of knowledge irrespective of distance or circumstance. On the Almajiri education system, the Sultan maintained that begging was prohibited in Islam, urging wealthy and privileged members of society to extend support to the less privileged and complement government efforts in addressing the challenges confronting vulnerable children. He acknowledged that government alone could not shoulder the entire responsibility of providing for the less privileged, stressing the need for collective action by individuals, communities and institutions. The Sultan also applauded Governor Yahaya for establishing modern Almajiri schools across Gombe State, describing the initiative as a positive step towards integrating religious and Western education and improving the learning opportunities available to Almajiri children. In his remarks, the Emir of Gombe, Alhaji Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, commended BOBA for drawing national attention to the challenge of out-of-school children and its implications for national security and development. He assured that the traditional institution would continue to collaborate with relevant organisations and stakeholders to promote education and improve access to learning opportunities, particularly across Northern Nigeria. Former Governor of Jigawa State and elder statesman, Sule Lamido, expressed concern over the state of Nigeria’s education system, warning that failure to address the crisis could create an environment in which vulnerable young people become susceptible to recruitment into criminal activities. Lamido called on political leaders at all levels to demonstrate the necessary political will to enact and implement strong legislation capable of revitalising the education sector, particularly in Northern Nigeria. Participants at the biennial lecture unanimously called for deliberate and sustained interventions by governments at all levels to revive the education system in the interest of national security, social stability and sustainable development. The event also featured goodwill messages from former Minister of Education, Hon. Aishatu Jibril Dukku, and Gombe State Commissioner for Education, Prof. Aishatu Maigari, who highlighted the achievements recorded by the Inuwa Yahaya administration in the education sector. items.title: SIAO 2026 : Entre satisfaction des visiteurs et difficultés commerciales des exposants
items.description: Après plusieurs jours d'activités, la 18e édition du Salon international de l'artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) a refermé ses portes ce samedi 7 novembre 2026. À l'heure du bilan, les appréciations sont partagées entre visiteurs et exposants. Si les premiers saluent globalement l'organisation et la diversité des produits proposés, les seconds évoquent des difficultés commerciales et quelques insuffisances dans les conditions d'exposition. Dans les différents pavillons du site du SIAO, les visiteurs ont pu découvrir une diversité de produits issus du savoir-faire artisanal africain. Objets de décoration, bijoux, articles en cuir, vêtements et produits locaux ont notamment constitué l'essentiel des découvertes. Pour plusieurs visiteurs, cette édition a été une expérience satisfaisante. C'est le cas d'Inès Ouédraogo, qui participait pour la première fois au rendez-vous avec ses enfants. Pour sa première participation au SIAO, Inès Ouédraogo se dit satisfaite de l'organisation. Elle apprécie particulièrement l'organisation générale et le dispositif sécuritaire. L'accès gratuit au site par les enfants de moins de 10 ans est l'innovation qui a retenu son attention. « Je trouve que l'organisation est assez bien ; et l'innovation majeure, c'est que les enfants de moins de 10 ans ne payent pas de ticket. J'étais bien contente. Les enfants aussi étaient contents de savoir qu'ils ne payaient pas pour entrer. Au niveau de la sécurité, je trouve que c'est assez bien organisé. On a accès facilement aux différents pavillons pour les visites. Donc, de mon côté, le bilan est positif », a-t-elle confié. Venue profiter des derniers moments du SIAO 2026, Axelle Ouédraogo retient notamment la diversité des productions exposées et les possibilités de rencontres professionnelles. « On a pu flâner et puis on a eu des contacts pour contacter certaines personnes pour les prochaines fois. Pour moi, c'était une très belle expérience et surtout on a constaté une innovation du côté des exposants du Burkina », a-t-elle expliqué. Axelle Ouédraogo effectuant quelques achats dans les stands du SIAO. Des contacts noués Plusieurs artisans rencontrés font état d'un marché difficile, lors des premiers jours du salon, mais qui s'est amélioré par la suite. Comme Issif Sawadogo, exposant venu de la Côte d'Ivoire et participant pour la quatrième fois au SIAO, qui estime que les affaires n'ont pas été faciles au début. Il constate néanmoins une amélioration des ventes au cours des derniers jours de la manifestation. Cependant, Issif Sawadogo affirme avoir noué de nouveaux partenariats, dont les effets pourraient se concrétiser après le salon. Pour lui, le SIAO ne doit pas uniquement être évalué à l'aune des ventes réalisées sur place, mais également en tenant compte des relations professionnelles nouées. « J'ai eu de nouveaux partenariats et après le SIAO, je pense qu'on va travailler ensemble. L'avantage, ce n'est pas seulement de venir vendre et repartir avec de l'argent. Il y a aussi des partenariats », a-t-il souligné. Le styliste-modéliste Issif Sawadogo est à sa quatrième participation au SIAO Salanon Thibo dit Dah Houwa est un exposant venu du Bénin. Spécialisé dans les produits biologiques, il partage ce constat. Selon lui, les clients étaient peu nombreux au début du salon, mais la situation s'est progressivement améliorée. Il invite les organisateurs à renforcer la communication autour de l'événement afin de toucher un public plus large. Il félicite l'organisation générale et le dispositif sécuritaire. « Tout est bien organisé sur le site. Il y a la sécurité partout. C'est nice », apprécie-t-il, le pouce levé. Exposant venu du Sénégal, Baye Fall évoque des partenariats noués au cours du salon. Venu du Sénégal, Baye Fall, quant à lui, affirme avoir noué quelques contacts. « Le marché est là. Les clients viennent, ils prennent un peu. Mais j'ai eu quelques contacts pour des partenariats », a-t-il conclu. Muriel Dominique Ouédraogo Lefaso.net

items.title: Gaza : les images choquantes d’enfants et de familles noyés sous de fortes pluies
items.description: Alors qu' Israël s’apprête à nommer pour la première fois un Premier ministre d’origine marocaine, le calvaire de la population de Gaza ne s'atténue pas. L'enclave palestinienne est noyée sous de fortes pluies, alors que les autorités israéliennes bloquent toujours le passage de l' aide humanitaire. La pluie emporte les tentes de fortune des Gazaouis Des pluies diluviennes s’abattent sur toute la Palestine, mais c’est la population de Gaza, dont une majeure partie vit sous des tentes, qui est affectée le plus. Selon les autorités locales de Gaza, les fortes pluies de samedi ont noyé au moins 70.000 tentes, faisant des dizaines de milliers de sans-abris. Gaza sous l'eau : les familles et leurs enfants face à des conditions dévastatrices https://t.co/uY0CBdLFu2 — TSA Algérie (@TSAlgerie) November 8, 2026 Les rues dévastées de l’enclave se sont transformées en torrents qui emportent tout et les murs et plafonds fragilisés par trois ans de bombardements israéliens se sont effondrés, faisant des victimes supplémentaires. Gaza. https://t.co/sJBwWlB92N — Aymeric Caron (@CaronAymericoff) November 7, 2026 Les rescapés de la guerre ont tout perdu, leurs tentes, leurs literies et leurs effets. « Mes enfants me demandent où nous allons passer la nuit. Je ne sais que leur répondre », a témoigné une mère de famille auprès de l’AFP. Appels à sauver le « peuple des tentes » à Gaza Dénuée de moyens, la défense civile locale est incapable de faire face à l'ampleur de la catastrophe. L’entrée de l'aide humanitaire, et notamment des tentes, est une urgence absolue. Des appels sont aussitôt lancés par des organisations locales et l’Autorité palestinienne pour faire pression sur Israël qui continue d'entraver l’entrée de l'aide humanitaire au mépris de l'accord de cessez-le-feu conclu il y a une année. De nombreuses organisations et observateurs ont mis en garde contre une catastrophe humanitaire imminente et le risque de propagation des épidémies. Les images qui parviennent de Gaza depuis samedi sont aussi impressionnantes que choquantes. On y voit des tentes entières emportées par les torrents avec tout ce qu'elles contiennent sur fond des cris désespérés de leurs propriétaires. « Tandis que nous dormons ce soir dans la chaleur de nos lits, il y a des enfants dont les murs sont le vent, qui s’allongent dans la boue et se couvrent de pluie, et ce pourrait bien être leur dernière nuit », a écrit l’écrivaine algérienne Ahlam Mosteghanemi dans un message émouvant sur X, appelant à ne pas oublier « le peuple des têtes ». C’est le quatrième hiver que les Gazaouis s'apprêtent à passer dans ces conditions. إخوتي في الإنسانية من كل الديانات السماوية ، لا تساهموا في إطفاء ضوء غزة . أذكروها و تذكّروها فهي يتيمة زماننا . بينما ننام الليلة في دفء أسرّتنا ، ثمّة أطفال جدرانهم الريح، يفترشون الوحل و يتدثرون بالمطر، قد تكون ليلتهم هذه الأخيرة « وأَنتَ تعودُ إلى البيت، بيِتكَ، فكِّرْ بغيركَ ، لا تنس شعب الخيامْ وأَنت تنام وتُحصي الكواكبَ، فكِّرْ بغيركَ ، ثَمَّةَ مَنْ لم يجد حيّزاً للمنام. » #محمود_درويش — أحلام مستغانمي (@AhlamMostghanmi) November 7, 2026 L’article Gaza : les images choquantes d’enfants et de familles noyés sous de fortes pluies est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 'Foolishness, misplaced over-smartness': Maryam removes Jhelum DC over exam postponement for her visit
items.description: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz removed the Jhelum deputy commissioner (DC) from his post on Sunday, after it emerged that computer science papers for intermediate students in the district had been postponed in the district owing to arrangements for the provincial chief executive’s scheduled visit on Nov 10. Originally scheduled for Nov 10, the computer science papers for the Intermediate Second Annual Examinations 2026 had been deferred on the recommendation of the now-dismissed Jhelum deputy commissioner, Mir Raza Ozgen. He wrote in a letter to the Rawalpindi Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) that due to the deployment of administrative and security personnel during the scheduled visit, “it is not feasible to ensure the smooth and uninterrupted conduct of the said examination in the district. It is, therefore, requested that the examination be postponed and rescheduled for another suitable date to avoid any inconvenience to students and ensure the smooth conduct of both the examination and the VVIP visit”. The move also came under scrutiny and criticism on social media. Eventually, Maryam posted on X that the Jhelum DC was being removed from his post with “immediate effect”. She said she had given “explicit instructions that no inconvenience or disruption whatsoever should be caused to the public during my visits to the districts”. “This is a clear disregard for my directions,” she added. In a subsequent post, she also shared a notification that said the DC had been transferred and was instructed to report to the Punjab Services and General Administration Department for further orders. Maryam also announced that the earlier postponed exams would now be held in line with the original schedule, on Nov 10. “Notwithstanding any acts of foolishness or misplaced over-smartness on part of the district administration, the examinations shall be held strictly in accordance with the original schedule, i.e. Tuesday, 10th November,” she posted on X. In another post on X, CM Maryam said she has directed all regional and district police officers as well as commissioners and deputy commissioners to ensure that “no market, shop, business, or any other establishment shall be closed or asked to suspend its operations on account of my visit.” She added that no residential streets will be blocked or sealed, or any restriction be placed on the movement of residents “under the pretext of security arrangements”. “Please ensure that all security measures are discreet and do not cause any inconvenience, disruption, or hardship to the general public,” she wrote, adding that the instructions must be “followed in letter and spirit”. “Failing to comply will result in strict action.”

items.title: Ebonyi govt lifts suspension on Ambertone as Ishiagu Community buries slain youths
items.description: By Chiamaka Ekwuwe The Ebonyi State Government has lifted the temporary suspension on mining operations at the Ambertone Logistics Limited facility, operated by Zotmann Mining Limited, in Ihetutu community, Ishiagu, Ivo Local Government Area, following consultations with relevant stakeholders and the burial of two youths who died in a shooting incident in the area. The resumption of operations on Wednesday followed days of engagements involving the state government, representatives of the mining company, bereaved families and community stakeholders aimed at restoring peace and normalcy. The development comes after the deaths of Chibuike Elema, 18, and Obinna Gideon Akandu, 20, in a shooting incident reportedly involving a military officer on Sunday, October 18, 2026. The precise circumstances surrounding the incident, including the events leading to the shooting and the responsibility of the personnel involved, remain subject to clarification by the appropriate authorities. Available accounts indicate that the incident occurred approximately three kilometres from the company’s operational facility, reportedly near another mining concession. Following the incident, tensions reportedly escalated in the community, with some youths allegedly attacking the mining company’s facility, resulting in damage to vehicles, equipment, offices and other property. In response to the developments and concerns over public safety, the Ebonyi State Government ordered a temporary suspension of mining activities at the affected facility to prevent further escalation and facilitate peace-building efforts. Following consultations and reconciliation engagements, the government subsequently announced the lifting of the suspension, allowing operations to resume. Ambertone, Zotmann Clarify Company Identity The incident also generated conflicting reports concerning the identity of the mining company operating the affected facility. While some initial reports associated the incident with Palladium Mining Company, subsequent clarification from company representatives identified Ambertone Logistics Limited as the company whose facility was affected by the unrest. Representatives further clarified that Palladium Mining Company operates a separate facility in the community and is distinct from Ambertone Logistics Limited and its operational partner, Zotmann Mining Limited. The clarification was issued to address confusion arising from reports that appeared to have linked Palladium Mining Company to the incident. Representatives of Ambertone and Zotmann also stated that neither company authorised the shooting, maintaining that the incident occurred outside their operational premises. The circumstances surrounding the shooting and any possible responsibility of individuals involved remain separate matters requiring appropriate investigation. Company’s Condolence Visit Paves Way for Reconciliation As part of efforts to promote reconciliation and rebuild confidence, representatives of Ambertone Logistics Limited visited the families of the two deceased youths to express condolences. The visit provided an opportunity for the families to communicate their concerns and for the company to express sympathy over the loss of the young men. Leading the delegation, Henry Onyeazor expressed sadness over the deaths, describing the incident as unfortunate and deeply regrettable. He conveyed the condolences of the company’s management and staff to the affected families, acknowledging the pain associated with losing loved ones at such young ages. Onyeazor said the visit was intended to demonstrate the company’s sympathy and commitment to maintaining peaceful relations with its host community. He also recalled the relationship between the company and Ihetutu community, noting that its operations had provided employment and economic opportunities for residents. Onyeazor appealed to community members to sustain peaceful engagement and avoid allowing the incident to undermine existing relationships. He also denied allegations that the company’s management instructed military personnel to shoot the youths. He maintained that the company had no interest in instigating violence against its host community and encouraged residents to allow the appropriate authorities to establish the facts surrounding the incident. Bereaved Family Appreciates Company’s Support Responding on behalf of the family of the late Chibuike Elema, his uncle, Elder Ukachukwu Josel Elema, appreciated the company representatives for visiting the family during its period of mourning. He described the death of his nephew as painful, particularly given his young age and the future that lay ahead of him. He said: “On behalf of my family, I sincerely appreciate the management of the company and everyone who has come here today to sympathise with us during this difficult period. “Death is a painful experience, particularly when it involves a young person whose future holds so much promise. We understand that no amount of tears, sorrow or mourning can bring back our beloved son.” The elder also expressed the family’s desire to understand the circumstances surrounding the shooting and called for clarity regarding the events that led to the deaths. He questioned why the young men were shot and stressed the importance of establishing what happened. He further acknowledged the relationship between the mining company and the community, noting that several residents benefited directly or indirectly from its activities. According to him, the family’s immediate priority had been to ensure that Chibuike’s remains were released for burial. He also expressed appreciation for the company’s presence and support during the family’s difficult period. Slain Youth’s Father Calls for Justice The father of the second victim, Hon. Joshua Akandu, a serving councillor representing Ihetutu Ward in Ishiagu, also received the company’s delegation. Akandu expressed profound grief over the death of his son, Obinna Gideon Akandu, describing the loss as devastating. During the visit, he received the delegation in accordance with local traditional customs and presented kola nuts. He also offered prayers, expressing his desire that anyone found responsible for his son’s death would be held accountable. His remarks reflected the family’s grief and its expectation that the circumstances surrounding the incident would be properly addressed. The engagement was regarded as part of the broader efforts to encourage dialogue and restore peaceful relations within the community. Ebonyi Government Lifts Suspension, Warns Mining Companies Announcing the lifting of the suspension, the Ebonyi State Commissioner for Solid Minerals, Mr. Chinedu Magnus Nkah, explained that the government had initially ordered the temporary closure of the affected facility as a precautionary measure to prevent further violence and protect lives and property. Nkah said the decision to permit the resumption of operations followed engagements involving the company, the bereaved families and other stakeholders. He confirmed that the deceased youths had been buried before the government announced the reopening. The commissioner also highlighted the economic importance of the mining operation to the host community, particularly its contribution to employment and the livelihoods of residents. He explained that the resumption would allow workers to return to their duties and support the restoration of economic activities affected by the temporary closure. However, Nkah issued a warning to mining companies operating across the state, stressing that the government would not tolerate violations of residents’ rights or any actions resulting in the loss of innocent lives. He emphasised that the protection of human life remained a priority of Governor Francis Nwifuru’s administration. The commissioner warned that mining companies found culpable in incidents involving the loss of residents’ lives, whether through their personnel or security arrangements, could face serious sanctions, including expulsion from the state. He maintained that economic benefits from mining activities could not take precedence over the safety and welfare of host communities. Ambertone, Zotmann Return to Operations as Peace Gradually Returns With the temporary suspension lifted and the two youths buried, attention has shifted towards restoring economic activities, rebuilding confidence and sustaining peaceful relations in Ihetutu community. For Ambertone Logistics Limited and Zotmann Mining Limited, the reopening of the facility marks the resumption of operations following the disruption caused by the incident and subsequent suspension. The companies have maintained that they neither authorised nor participated in the shooting, while their representatives have emphasised that the incident reportedly occurred outside their operational premises. The government’s decision to lift the suspension represents an administrative step towards restoring normalcy and allowing economic activities to resume. However, the reopening should not be interpreted as a determination of the circumstances surrounding the shooting or a substitute for any investigation that may be required. Ultimately, the priority remains the establishment of the facts, accountability where responsibility is established, protection of host communities and the promotion of responsible mining operations across Ebonyi State. The post Ebonyi govt lifts suspension on Ambertone as Ishiagu Community buries slain youths appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: President Mahama urges the church to mentor the youth and support job creation
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has called on professionals, entrepreneurs and artisans in the Assemblies of God, Ghana, to mentor young people and support them to acquire employable skills. He said the Church could help address youth unemployment by creating apprenticeship and business development opportunities for young people. The President appealed to the second induction service of Reverend Stephen Yenusom Wengam as General Superintendent of the Assemblies of God, Ghana, and the outdooring of the Church’s new Executive Presbytery officers in Accra. He said many young people were striving to build their future but continued to face uncertainty over employment and the cost of establishing independent lives, adding that their concerns deserved greater attention and that their skills and talents required opportunities to develop. “I encourage the professionals in our Church, entrepreneurs and artisans, to make time for them. Mentor a young person. Offer an apprenticeship where possible,” he said. President Mahama urged established professionals and business owners to guide young people on how to build sustainable enterprises. “Help a young person understand how to start a sustainable business. Such liberal actions can change the course of their lives,” he said. The President said the Church’s men’s ministry, women’s ministry and other departments had important roles to play in supporting young people as they navigated the challenges of adulthood. He said Church members should model responsible behaviour and demonstrate the values they sought to instil in the next generation. President Mahama said the Church’s transformation agenda provided an opportunity to deepen its contribution to society through community engagement and support for vulnerable groups. He congratulated Rev. Wengam and the newly inducted executive officers, saying leadership should be viewed as service and exercised in the interest of those being served. Rev. Wengam called on the Government to ensure that economic recovery translated into jobs, improved incomes and business growth. He said although the economy was showing signs of recovery, its benefits needed to reach ordinary Ghanaians, particularly unemployed youth. “Now that the recovery must mean decent jobs for our young people, better incomes for our farmers, and room for our businesses to grow and hire,” he said. Rev. Wengam described youth unemployment as “heart-rending and soul-wrenching”, saying many young people continued to struggle to secure jobs. He expressed the hope that the Government’s economic recovery programme would expand opportunities for unemployed youth and others facing economic challenges. Rev. Wengam said the Church remained committed to its transformation agenda, which focused on human resource development, pastoral welfare, infrastructure and evangelism. He said the Assemblies of God, Ghana, had planted 2,077 churches over the past four years, increasing membership from 812,254 to about 1.2 million. Rev. Wengam said the Church would intensify its local and international missionary activities during his second term, including expanding outreach to countries where it had no presence. The event was attended by government officials, ministers of state, gospel musicians and other high-ranking dignitaries.

items.title: ‘How UK universities generate billions from Nigerian brains’
items.description: …as ‘Nigerian universities generate certificates the economy cannot use’ By Egufe Yafugborhi There is a painful paradox haunting Nigeria’s ivory towers. The same Nigerian professor who struggles to get his research paper published at home becomes a patent holder, a company founder and a billion-dollar value creator once he lands in Oxford, Cambridge or London. Why? Rights activist and Coordinator, Niger Delta Peace Coalition, Zik Gbemre, in a recent travel appraisal, provided the blunt answer in his findings capped, ‘Why UK Universities Generate Billions While Local Academics Struggle At Home’. Gbemre noted: “There is an ongoing debate about the productivity of Nigerian universities and their academic staff. “Compare top UK institutions such as the University of Oxford, University of Cambridge, and University College London (UCL) to Nigerian universities, the difference in financial contribution and job creation is staggering”. The activist puts figures to the debate: “A single top university in the UK like Cambridge generates around £30 billion (38 billion USD) annually for the UK economy and supports over 86,000 direct and indirect jobs. “Put that into context: The economic output of just two or three top UK universities combined exceeds the entire annual national budgets of most West African nations.” The question then is not whether Nigerian academics are brilliant. They are. The question is why that brilliance does not translate to wealth at home. According to Gbemre, the answer lies in how UK universities make money. “Unlike local institutions that rely almost entirely on government budget allocations or basic tuition, UK universities operate as high-value commercial enterprise hubs. They generate wealth through five main streams,” he explains. He lists them: “Patent Licensing & Royalties: Universities own the patents to scientific discoveries made in their labs. “Global corporations pay millions in royalties to use these inventions.” “Spin-Out Companies: When professors discover a breakthrough (like a new drug or algorithm), the university creates a real business around it. UK university spin-outs generate over £12 billion annually and hire thousands of people. “High-Value Industry Contracts: Companies like Rolls-Royce, Pfizer, and Boeing pay universities millions to conduct specialized research or use their advanced lab equipment. “Education as an Export: International students pay premium tuition. Beyond tuition, they spend billions on housing, food, transport, and local businesses. “Endowments & Investments: Wealthy institutions invest billions in real estate, venture capital, and stock markets, earning millions in passive returns every year.” Nigeria in reverse model In Nigeria, the model is reversed. Universities wait for allocation. They collect tuition that barely covers diesel. Research ends in a library shelf. The second big difference, Gbemre argues, is what a job really means in the varsity system. “The UK university model creates productive, high-value jobs rather than administrative seats created just to fill portfolios,” he says. He is specific: “Technology Transfer Managers: Experts who turn academic research into commercial patents and negotiate deals with private companies. “Lab Scientists & Researchers: Staff funded directly by private industry grants to develop market-ready products. “Incubator Leads & Venture Directors: Professionals who run university business hubs and connect student/professor startups with venture capital investors.” The multiplier effect is huge. “Every direct job at a top UK university generates roughly 2.8 additional external jobs in the local economy (suppliers, contractors, spin-out staff, and service providers)”, Gbemre measures. In Nigeria, one appointment often generates one chair and one table, and a queue of personal assistants. But Gbemre saves his harshest critique for the attitude and incentive problem. “Is it poor salaries or bad attitude?” he asks. “The reality behind why Nigerian academics shine abroad but struggle at home comes down to a mix of attitude, incentives, and infrastructure.” He explains the contrasting incentive structures. “Abroad, academics are judged on funding secured, patents registered, and industry problems solved. At home, academic promotion has historically favored years served, internal politics, and publishing papers that sit on shelves. “Lacking Ecosystem: You cannot commercialize research without Technology Transfer Offices (TTOs), functional laboratories, reliable power, and venture capital partnerships. Without these, even brilliant ideas die. “Workplace Culture: Entrenched bureaucracy, resistance to modern performance tracking, and a mindset focused on entitlement rather than value creation heavily hinder productivity.” It is not that Nigerians are less hardworking. “Nigerian academics are not naturally unproductive; the system they operate in at home rewards paper titles over tangible economic value,” Gbemre says. And he concludes with a warning: “Until Nigerian higher education shifts from a ‘degree factory’ model to a ‘commercial innovation hub’ model, universities will continue to drain resources rather than generate wealth.” That shift is the challenge in Nigeria. Imagine if the University of Benin owned the patent for a malaria breakthrough and earned royalties from every drug sold in Africa. Imagine if Delta State University churns out a fisheries technology company from its research in the creeks. Imagine if University of Lagos had venture directors connecting student coders to investors instead of only lecturers reading notes from 1989. The brain is the same. The Nigerian professor in Cambridge and the one in Abraka both passed through the same secondary school rigour, same JAMB stress. One landed in a system that says, “What problem have you solved that industry will pay for?” The other landed in a system that says, “How many years have you served and who do you know in the Senate?” Until that incentive changes, Gbemre harps that UK universities will continue to generate billions from Nigerian brains, while Nigerian universities continue to generate certificates that the economy cannot use. The post ‘How UK universities generate billions from Nigerian brains’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Locally built robots serve taste of future to Karachi diners
items.description: Wheeling its way between dining booths at a neon-lit restaurant in Karachi, a robot waitress drops off a fresh pizza to an awaiting family. While global buzz is growing around agile humanoids made in the United States, China and elsewhere, robotic staff are a rare sight in the South Asian country. “Welcome to Sicilian. My name is Robia,” the waitress says in an electronic voice, looking down at diners through blinking red LED eyes. This photograph taken on October 2, 2026 shows Robia (R) and Jojo (2R), humanoid robot waitresses serving customers at The Sicilian restaurant in Karachi. — AFP Robia and her colleague Jojo are the DIY creations of Pakistani engineer Syed Osama Aziz, who is bringing a sci-fi reboot to Karachi’s storied dining scene. They have spherical white heads and dark visors, similar to a motorcycle helmet, and sport black shawls around their neck in the style of a dupatta . Aziz, who also established The Sicilian restaurant, developed the machines using mostly locally manufactured parts, designing their circuit boards and programming them in his own lab. “The equipment, the things needed to make robots, are not so easily available here, so we had to arrange them,” he told AFP . This photograph taken on September 30, 2026 shows a robotics software engineer Syed Osama Aziz working on robot components at his workshop in Multan. — AFP The duo were developed through his robotics company, Cobot, with help from friends and some electronic components imported from abroad. In China and other East Asian countries especially, robots are an increasingly common sight , shuttling food to customers in chain restaurants and taking on other jobs from cleaning to greeting hotel guests. But they remain a novelty in Pakistan, where Aziz’s home-grown creations are attracting curious diners. When they arrive at a table, the customers must either take the food off their serving tray themselves or wait for a human member of staff to assist them. This photograph taken on October 2, 2026 shows a staff passing food orders to Robia, a humanoid robot waitress at The Sicilian restaurant in Karachi. — AFP Excited customers Aziz, whose workshop manufacturing the robots is located in Multan, hopes to make his creations more sophisticated in the future. “Our plans are to add camera-based processing and image-processing features,” he said. “That means the robot will also recognise you by looking at you, and it will remember what you ordered last time, and accordingly it will be able to give you better suggestions.” For now, the robots are proving a hit with families, who flock to the restaurant to watch the machines in action. This photograph taken on October 2, 2026 shows children playing around Robia, a humanoid robot waitress at The Sicilian restaurant in Karachi. — AFP “The best thing about it is that it introduces itself,” excited customer Ahmer Zameer told AFP , explaining the robot also “tells you what things you can order”. Children reach out to touch the robots while their parents snap photographs and selfies. Young customer Sonia Dilosker said she was impressed by the androids’ appearance and preferred their approach to serving customers, “because it is a machine and without any emotions”. Restaurant staff say the novelty has brought a surge in customers — some travelling from across the sprawling port city to meet the robots. This photograph taken on October 2, 2026 shows Robia, a humanoid robot waitress serving customers at The Sicilian restaurant in Karachi. — AFP “Our business has grown. People are coming from far away for this. They have seen a robot for the first time here,” staff member Hellen told AFP . “People are excited to see this.” Header image: This photograph taken on October 2, 2026 shows Robia, a humanoid robot waitress serving customers at The Sicilian restaurant in Karachi. — AFP

items.title: Sky Train trial: Former GIIF CEO seeks court order to compel 15 persons to testify
items.description: The first accused person in the ongoing Sky Train trial, Solomon Asamoah, has asked the court to compel 15 individuals, including former government officials, directors of the Ghana Infrastructure Investment Fund (GIIF), and financial experts, to testify in his defence. Deputy Attorney-General Justice Srem-Sai disclosed this in a Facebook post, saying the accused persons had indicated that they had no witnesses but that Mr Asamoah wanted the court to order the 15 individuals to appear and testify on his behalf. The list includes former Minister for Railway Development Joe Ghartey, the Chief Executive Officer of GIIF, Nana Dwemoh Benneh, the Auditor-General, Dr Pamela Graham, and representatives of Deloitte Ghana and PricewaterhouseCoopers. The case involves Mr. Asamoah and former Board Chairman Professor Christopher Ameyaw-Akumfi, who are standing trial over an alleged US$2 million financial loss to the state linked to the proposed Accra Sky Train project. The prosecution alleges that the two former officials conspired to cause financial loss to the Republic by facilitating the payment of US$2 million to Africa Investor Holdings Limited, a company linked to the proposed urban rail project, without the requisite approval from the GIIF Board. The payment was reportedly made in February 2019 for an equity stake in a company associated with the project. The proposed Sky Train was intended to provide an elevated urban rail transportation system in Accra to help address traffic congestion. The project was expected to be developed through a partnership involving the government, GIIF and private-sector investors. However, the railway system was never constructed. The prosecution has maintained that the transaction was not approved by the GIIF Board and that the funds were disbursed without the necessary authorisation. The two accused persons have pleaded not guilty to six charges, including conspiracy to wilfully cause financial loss to the Republic, wilfully causing financial loss and conspiracy to commit intentional dissipation of public funds. The prosecution closed its case in May 2026 after calling three witnesses. In July 2026, the High Court dismissed a submission of no case filed by the accused persons, ruling that they had to open their defence. The court subsequently directed them to file their witness statements, which were submitted in September 2026.

items.title: Le SG du RND rassure : « La pomme de terre d’El Oued arrive »
items.description: La pomme de terre continue d’occuper les devants de la scène en Algérie, qui est le deuxième producteur africain de ce tubercule avec 4,6 millions de tonnes par an. Après le gouvernement, c’est autour d’un parti politique de s’exprimer sur cette crise qui préoccupe les Algériens depuis plusieurs jours. Le secrétaire général du RND, Monder Bouden, a tenté de rassurer les consommateurs, depuis Constantine. « Nous avons remarqué que les prix de la pomme de terre dans les marchés de gros vont de 130 à 140 dinars le kilogramme alors qu’elle est presque introuvable auprès des commerces de détail », a déclaré le secrétaire général du RND, Monder Bouden, lors d’un meeting qu’il a animé samedi à Constantine. « Cette période de l’année connaît toujours des perturbations dans l’approvisionnement des marchés en pomme de terre », a-t-il rappelé, en estimant que cette situation ne va pas durer. « Le gouvernement a décidé de libérer le stock national en pomme de terre pour approvisionner les marchés avec 7.000 tonnes chaque semaine », a-t-il annoncé. Cela en attendant l’arrivée de la récolte d’El Oued, dont la production annuelle de la pomme de terre est estimée à plus de 1,6 million de tonnes. « Nous rassurons les citoyens que, dans environ 15 jours, la récolte d’Oued Souf arrivera sur les marchés et les choses rentreront dans l’ordre », a affirmé le SG du RND. Sifi Ghrieb : « Nous ne tolérons aucune spéculation » Cette énième crise de la pomme de terre est intervenue après le plafonnement de son prix, fixé par le gouvernement, en début octobre dernier, entre 80 et 90 DA le kilogramme. Une décision prise pour freiner la hausse de ce produit de large consommation dans un contexte où les agriculteurs bénéficient de plusieurs subventions publiques qui couvrent, entre autres, l’électricité, les engrais et l’eau. Le plafonnement du prix de ce produit de large consommation a, apparemment, fait réagir les spéculateurs qui tentent, à travers cette pénurie, de résister pour conserver leurs intérêts. Jeudi dernier, le Premier ministre Sifi Ghrieb a usé de mots forts pour mettre en garde les spéculateurs. « Nous ne tolérons plus la spéculation et nous utiliserons tous les moyens pour la combattre. Nous utiliserons les méthodes les plus extrêmes que l’on peut imaginer. Nous ne tolérons aucune manipulation qui touche le panier du citoyen », a averti Sifi Ghrieb. L’article Le SG du RND rassure : « La pomme de terre d’El Oued arrive » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Yoruba started home video, not Nollywood — Osuofia
items.description: Veteran Nollywood actor, Nkem Owoh, popularly known as Osuofia, has clarified his position on the origins of Nigeria’s home-video industry, insisting that Yoruba filmmakers pioneered home-video productions but did not start Nollywood. Owoh made the clarification during an appearance on Curiosity Made Me Ask, hosted by comedian and content creator Adebayo Abidemi, popularly known as Bae U. The interview, published on the host’s YouTube channel on Saturday, featured the actor responding to a question about reports that he had claimed Yoruba people, rather than the Igbo, started Nollywood. The clarification comes amid an ongoing debate over the contributions of different ethnic groups to the development of Nigeria’s film industry. The debate gained fresh attention in August 2026 when late veteran actor Francis Duru argued that the Igbo built Nollywood but that Yoruba filmmakers had become more dominant because of their ability to organise and promote their productions. Duru, who died in October, had attributed much of the growth of the modern home-video industry in the 1990s and early 2000s to Igbo entrepreneurs. Reacting to the reported interpretation of his earlier comments, Owoh said it was inaccurate to suggest that he claimed Yoruba people started Nollywood, explaining that the name did not exist when filmmakers began producing movies. “First of all, you have given me this wrong accusation that I said, Yoruba started Nollywood. No. Yoruba started this film on… when did Nollywood come out? When we started the thing, there was no Nollywood as a name. “We sat together and we’re banding, you know, ideas and all that, how the thing is going to come to fruition. And eventually, we chose Nollywood,” he said. The actor, however, credited Yoruba filmmakers with popularising home-video productions in Nigeria, specifically mentioning veteran filmmaker Hubert Ogunde and Adebayo Papa as among those whose works he admired. “So, Yoruba started the thing. They made the thing very popular home video and all that. Yes, they did. And I’ve said it several. Okay. Ogunde and Adebayo Papa. These are the people I love to watch their thing,” he said. When the interviewer jokingly suggested that Ogunde was Igbo, Owoh disagreed, insisting that the late filmmaker was Yoruba. “Ogunde is not Igbo. I’m telling you that Yoruba started it. When Ogunde was out, I don’t think there was any Igbo man who was that popular in that,” he added. He further emphasised the distinction between the origins of home-video productions and Nollywood, stating: “The Yoruba did not start Nollywood. They started Home video.” Historical accounts of Nigerian cinema trace the development of Yoruba filmmaking to travelling theatre groups led by figures such as Hubert Ogunde and Duro Ladipo, whose stage productions evolved into film and video productions decades before the commercial home-video boom of the 1990s. However, the emergence of the modern commercial direct-to-video market is widely associated with the 1992 Igbo-language film Living in Bondage, produced by Kenneth Nnebue, which helped popularise the format and laid the foundation for the industry later known globally as Nollywood. The name Nollywood itself emerged years after the early home-video productions, as the Nigerian film industry gained wider recognition internationally. Owoh’s clarification has added another dimension to the longstanding debate over the respective contributions of Yoruba and Igbo filmmakers to the evolution of Nigerian cinema. items.title: Israël | Ce que la désignation d’Eisenkot doit aux électeurs arabes
items.description: Les dix-neuf sièges arabes conquis le 27 octobre dernier ont produit leur premier effet institutionnel. Le 7 novembre, le président Isaac Herzog a annoncé qu’il confiait à Gadi Eisenkot la charge de former le prochain gouvernement d’Israël ; le mandat lui est remis ce 8 novembre. Sa décision repose sur soixante-sept recommandations, contre quarante-six pour Benjamin Netanyahu. Abdelhamid Larguèche * Or ces soixante-sept n’existent pas sans les dix-neuf. Les quarante-huit députés de l’opposition sioniste ne suffisaient pas à faire une majorité. Ce sont le Ra’am de Mansour Abbas, puis la Liste commune à l’unanimité, qui ont fait basculer le rapport de forces, tandis que le Judaïsme unifié de la Torah, allié de longue date de Netanyahou, choisissait de ne recommander personne. L’acte est institutionnel, sa portée est historique. Depuis 1948, la vie politique israélienne s’est organisée autour d’une règle non écrite : les décisions qui engagent l’avenir de l’État doivent reposer sur une «majorité juive» . Les citoyens arabes votaient et siégeaient, mais leur suffrage restait tenu à la lisière de la décision. Yitzhak Rabin en fit l'expérience en 1995 : l'accord d’Oslo II ne fut approuvé, par 61 voix contre 59, que grâce aux députés arabes, et la droite lui contesta aussitôt toute légitimité. En 2018, la loi fondamentale sur l'État-nation du peuple juif a inscrit cette hiérarchie dans l’ordre constitutionnel, en réservant au seul peuple juif le droit à l’autodétermination nationale. Une majorité reconnue, pas encore gouvernante En désignant le candidat d’une majorité qui n’existe que par les voix arabes, le chef de l’État ne fait qu’appliquer la procédure. Mais en l’appliquant, il désavoue la doctrine qui a longtemps tenu lieu de constitution politique. Le Likoud l’a compris, qui avait mis en garde le président contre tout gouvernement dépendant des partis arabes. Il faut pourtant se garder de confondre recommandation et coalition. Eisenkot dispose de vingt-huit jours, prolongeables de quatorze, pour former un gouvernement ; d’ici là, Netanyahu demeure Premier ministre. Dans son propre camp, Avigdor Liberman et Naftali Bennett refusent un gouvernement dépendant des formations arabes, et Liberman écarte même un gouvernement minoritaire soutenu de l’extérieur. Eisenkot, lui, subordonne tout partenariat à ses conditions : conscription universelle, reconnaissance d’Israël comme État juif, qualification du Hamas comme organisation terroriste. La Liste commune a recommandé Eisenkot sans vouloir siéger au gouvernement ; Ahmad Tibi a prévenu que «sans les partis arabes, il n’y aura pas de changement» . L’histoire récente invite à la prudence. En mars 2020, Benny Gantz avait déjà reçu le mandat grâce à des recommandations incluant la Liste commune, avant de s’en détourner pour gouverner avec Netanyahu. Une désignation ne fait pas tomber un mur. Israël | Pourquoi l’alliance de l’opposition avec les partis arabes est-elle si compliquée ? La brèche et le mur Ce qui distingue pourtant le moment présent tient au poids inédit de dix-neuf sièges, à l’unanimité des deux formations arabes et à l’expérience acquise depuis l’entrée de Ra’am au gouvernement en 2021. Il tient surtout à un rapport de forces qui rend l’autre voie coûteuse : un gouvernement d’union avec le Likoud reviendrait à reconduire, sous un autre nom, le pouvoir que les électeurs viennent de désavouer. La fin des ségrégations ethno-religieuses ne se décrétera pas à la résidence présidentielle. Elle suppose que le suffrage arabe cesse d’être une force d’appoint pour devenir un plein droit de cité : association aux décisions, révision des lois qui hiérarchisent les citoyens selon leur appartenance, de la loi sur la propriété des absents à celle sur l’État-nation, égalité budgétaire, sécurité dans les localités arabes. Les conditions d’Eisenkot montrent combien le cadre ethno-national reste la norme jusque dans le camp dit «du changement.» Mais les ségrégations ne cèdent jamais d’un coup. Elles reculent lorsqu’une majorité découvre qu’elle ne peut plus gouverner sans ceux qu’elle tenait à l’écart. Le 27 octobre, les Palestiniens d’Israël ont montré qu’on n’efface pas un peuple qui vote. Le mandat du 8 novembre pose à Israël la question inverse : saura-t-il gouverner avec lui ? * Historien. items.title: Wembley Sports Construction’s Robert Coleman gifts Nathaniel Attoh GHC 50,000
items.description: Wembley Sports Construction Chief Executive Officer Robert Coleman has rewarded JoySports journalist Nathaniel Attoh with GHC 50,000 following his emergence as the 2026 Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Sports Journalist of the Year. Coleman announced the cash gift at the 30th GJA Awards ceremony in Accra on Saturday, November 7, in recognition of Attoh’s outstanding contribution to sports journalism. Attoh, affectionately known as Citizen Attoh, beat Media General’s Bill Eshun to win the prestigious award, earning recognition for his documentary, The Audacious Leap . The documentary, which premiered on JoyNews on May 19, 2025, tells the story of Ghanaian para-athlete Gilbert Ampiah and his determination to overcome physical challenges to pursue his athletics ambitions. At the time of production, Ampiah was a 16-year-old student at St Augustine’s College in Cape Coast, where he was making remarkable progress as a high jumper despite being born with a leg deformity. For the documentary, Attoh visited the school and spoke to people who had played important roles in the teenager’s development, including his father, teachers, trainers and colleagues. Ampiah has since established himself as one of Ghana’s promising junior para-athletes, with ambitions of competing at the highest level internationally. His training performances ahead of the 2025 inter-schools competition attracted widespread attention on social media, bringing greater visibility to his talent and determination. Among his notable achievements was clearing 1.60 metres at Ekumfi Atwa in 2023, where he competed against able-bodied athletes. He later set a personal best of 1.82 metres at the inter-house competition at St Augustine’s College. His progress has also extended to the international stage, where he won bronze in the High Jump T44 category at the Crown Prince Moulay El Hassan International Para Athletics Meeting in Marrakech, Morocco. Ampiah cleared 1.73 metres to secure his first international medal. Attoh’s recognition continues JoySports’ remarkable run at the GJA Awards, with the journalist becoming the third consecutive winner from the Multimedia Group’s sports desk. He follows Muftawu Nabila Abdulai, who won the Sports Journalist of the Year award in 2024 and 2025.
