items.title: FCC on workplace harassment
items.description: THE commentary that followed the recent Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) judgement dismissing the harassment claim of an NBP employee gives the impression that the court has rolled back the scope of the workplace harassment law so that it now covers only incidents of an ove­r­tly sexual nature, excluding conduct that amounts to gender-based discrimination. This is incorrect. The correct position of the law now is this: allegations of workplace harassment prior to 2022 (which is when the Protection Against Harassment of Women in the Workplace Act was amended) must involve conduct of an overtly sexual nature to fall within the scope of the law. Actions that take place after the 2022 amendment are covered by the law not only if they are overtly sexual in nature, but also if they are rooted in gender-based discrimination. Let’s see why. First, let’s look at the definition of ‘harassment’. Prior to January 2022, it was defined to cover “any unwelcome sexual advance, request for sexual favours or other verbal or written communication or physical conduct of a sexual nature or sexually demeaning attitudes, causing interference with work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment, or the attempt to punish the complainant for refusal to comply to such a request or is made a condition for employment”. This definition was amended in January 2022 by adding the following: “discrimination on basis of gender, which may or may not be sexual in nature, but which may embody a discriminatory and prejudicial mindset or notion, resulting in discriminatory behaviour on basis of gender against the complainant” (Section 2[h][ii] of the Act). The court interpreted the original definition restrictively, following the reasoning of the first Nadia Naz judgement. The amendment was made after the 2021 Supreme Court decision in Nadia Naz vs President of Pakistan . This case, which analysed and applied the original, pre-2022 definition of harassment, concluded that the law only covers harassment of an overtly sexual nature. The 2022 amendment, passed a few months after the judgement, rectified the limitation in the original definition as interpreted by the Supreme Court in the Nadia Naz judgement of 2021. The amended definition explicitly includes gender-based discrimination within the meaning of harassment. The amended definition would not apply retrospectively. The expanded definition, which broadens the scope of the actionable wrong, would only cover actions that take place after the amendment. But in 2023 the Supreme Court, reviewing the Nadia Naz judgement, held that the original definition was broad enough to include gender-based discrimination. Harassment as originally defined should be interpreted to include conduct that is not overtly sexual in nature but amounts to gender-based discrimination. The Supreme Court declared that the bench’s interpretation of the original definition was too restrictive. The interpretation in the Nadia Naz judgement on review would be brilliant were it not for the 2022 amendment. By interpreting the original definition to have essentially the same meaning and effect as the 2022 insertion, the Supreme Court implies that the 2022 amendment was redundant. This contradicts a basic principle of statutory interpretation, which requires that each statutory provision should be interpreted to give it a distinct meaning. It may well be that the 2022 amendment was not needed because the original definition should be interpreted as broadly and purposively as the Supreme Court did in the Nadia Naz judgement on review. But when the legislature amended the definition in 2022 to explicitly cover gender-based discrimination, it also implied that the earlier definition was restrictive, which is why the amendment was needed. By explicitly expanding the de­­finition, it endorsed the view that the original definition did not cover gender-based discrimination. The FCC in its recent judgement did the same. The FCC interpreted the original definition restrictively, following the reasoning of the first Nadia Naz judgement. It did not refer to the 2022 amendment, and it did not need to because the incidents involved in the case predated the amendment. The amended definition would not apply to these facts. It would have been more edifying if the FCC had clearly explained this, but lucid, well-written judgements are unfortunately uncommon. Let’s say, as many have argued, that the FCC should have interpreted the original definition more broadly to include gender-based discrimination. What implication would that have for the current definition of harassment? Such an interpretation would entail that the second part of the definition is redundant because the first part covers conduct embodying gender-based discrimination. Such reasoning would again contradict the principle of statutory interpretation, which says that the legislature does not waste its words. The FCC decision is deeply flawed, but for another reason. The FCC has not applied its own interpretation properly. The harassment at issue in this case was overtly sexual in nature. The evidence put forward at the earlier stages of the case, before the Islamabad High Court and the ombudsperson, shows that the complainant faced harassment that was unambiguously sexual. It is disturbing that the FCC did not consider this conduct to fall within the scope of the original definition. Flawed as it is, the FCC has not overruled the 2022 amendment to the law. The expanded definition (Section 2(h)(ii)) still stands, but it will only apply to incidents that took place or are alleged to have taken place after the date of the amendment. Prior incidents will be covered by the original definition, which will be interpreted restrictively. This clarification is important because after the FCC ruling and the outrage against it, many potential claimants believe that the pervasive gender-based discrimination they currently face at the workplace is not covered by the law. People sitting on workplace harassment committees have told me that their mandate is now restricted to only incidents that are overtly sexual in nature. We must remind them that it is not. The writer is a lawyer and the author of Progressive Laws In Patriarchal Societies. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Alberto Núñez Feijóo: “Hacer una coalición de Gobierno con Vox no depende de mí”
items.description: El presidente del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, de 65 años, lidera las encuestas para las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. Pero esos mismos sondeos señalan que, a estas alturas, solo podría gobernar con apoyo de Vox. El posible pacto con la formación ultraderechista , su arquitectura y la distribución de poder que acarrearía se han vuelto una de las piedras de toque de esta campaña. Feijóo, un político veterano que presidió la Xunta de Galicia desde abril de 2009 hasta mayo de 2022, es consciente de ese nudo e incluso detalla las líneas rojas que impondría, pero aún antepone lograr una mayoría suficiente en las urnas y evitar tener socios en el Consejo de Ministros. Lo que en ningún caso contempla es pedir la abstención del PSOE para gobernar sin Vox: Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sánchez se sube a la ola de resistencia progresista americana
items.description: Los dos grandes cuarteles generales de la política española, el del PP y el PSOE, tienen una enorme diferencia de enfoque en un tema central: la política internacional. En el PP creen que prácticamente nadie en España va a votar mirando a lo que pasa fuera. Están convencidos, según explican varios de sus miembros, de que las elecciones se deciden en asuntos puramente españoles o con claro componente local: el antisanchismo , la corrupción, Ceuta , el accidente de Urda, la amnistía, el nacionalismo, Bildu, la inmigración, la okupación. Su líder, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, apenas habla de asuntos internacionales y no se mueve cómodo ahí. Pero el PP no parece preocupado por esa cuestión. “Ahí no se juegan las elecciones”, insisten. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Iñaki Barrón: “El ferrocarril tiene mucho que envidiar en seguridad al modo aéreo, sobre todo en entrenamiento”
items.description: El ingeniero de Caminos Iñaki de Barrón (Zaragoza, 70 años) observa el siniestro ferroviario de Urda (Toledo) desde una posición de larga experiencia en el ferrocarril. Le respaldan 34 años de gestión en Renfe, hasta 2021; haber sido una figura relevante en la Unión Internacional de Ferrocarriles, y su cargo de presidente de la Comisión de Investigación de Accidentes Ferroviarios (CIAF) hasta julio, teniendo como última encomienda de calado el análisis del accidente de Adamuz (Córdoba), también en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla. Actúa ahora como portavoz del Comité de Seguimiento del Accidente de Urda en el Colegio de Ingenieros de Caminos, en cuya sede de Madrid se realiza esta entrevista el pasado jueves, y aconseja una auditoría exhaustiva en la alta velocidad tras estimar en 10.000 millones el esfuerzo necesario en mantenimiento para los próximos diez años. Esa cifra no solo multiplica las previstas por el Gobierno (que van de los 435 millones presupuestados en 2025 a los 628 para 2030), sino que excluye el gasto imprescindible para poner al día la red convencional que usan los trenes de Cercanías y mercancías: ahí el problema es “peor”, advierte. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Trump cae derrotado en las urnas, pero aún es poderoso (e impredecible) en política exterior
items.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ya es un pato cojo, el nombre con el que se conoce en la jerga política de Washington a los líderes que no pueden ser reelegidos. Si fuera otro mandatario, cabría esperar de él que, tras la derrota de su partido en las elecciones de mitad de mandato , se centrara cada vez más en la política exterior e intentara lograr alguna ambiciosa meta de paz y entendimiento mundial: una forma de tratar de apuntalar su legado y de recibir aún en el exterior un respeto y una pompa que van disminuyendo en su territorio nacional. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mucho debate y pocas risas: El humor político no logra el salto televisivo nacional desde ‘Polònia’ o ‘Vaya semanita’
items.description: El éxito autonómico de Polònia empezó con un fracaso nacional. En octubre de 2005, Toni Soler y su equipo trasladaron las imitaciones y parodias políticas del radiofónico Minoría absoluta a Antena 3 en Mire usté . Zapatero, Rajoy, el Estatut, Carod Rovira… todos se cruzaban en sketches en otra candente época política, pero a España su humor no le hizo mucha gracia. Con un 17,9% de audiencia en prime time (que cualquiera firmaría hoy) desapareció de la parrilla tras ocho programas . Al periodista y a su equipo, sin embargo, les hicieron una llamada desde casa: el programa había tenido éxito en Cataluña, y querían replicarlo en TV3. En estos 20 años, no han mirado atrás. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las mujeres pierden terreno en la empresa y la política tras décadas de progreso
items.description: La presencia de las mujeres en puestos de poder ha retrocedido en el mundo, en los últimos años, tras décadas de progreso. Ha ocurrido en el mundo de la empresa y de la política; y tanto en Estados Unidos, como en España y el conjunto de Europa; en paralelo a una ola reaccionaria contra el feminismo y su última explosión, el Me Too, que, en cualquier caso, nunca logró la igualdad. El martes, en las elecciones legislativas estadounidenses, un número récord de mujeres ganó escaño en la Cámara de Representantes , pero este hito no altera la fotografía global: la hegemonía masculina se ha consolidado y reforzado incluso en múltiples ámbitos de liderazgo y representación. Según el consenso de las expertas —aquí sí hay una aplastante mayoría femenina—, el golpe a las políticas de diversidad, muy alentado por la segunda victoria trumpista , ha dado combustible a los viejos patrones de conducta e inercias discriminatorias. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Después de lo ‘woke’?
items.description: Hace diez años, Donald Trump recibió a Nigel Farage en su torre de la Quinta Avenida, y el calendario ha querido que el aniversario de aquella fotografía llegue la misma semana en que los estadounidenses le han infligido una derrota histórica. Los dos hombres que sacudieron la política en nombre de la gente corriente posaban sonrientes junto a un ascensor dorado. ¿Cómo un multimillonario rodeado de oro podía erigirse como representante de los olvidados? Trump no se parece en nada a un trabajador de Ohio, pero sus votantes no le pedían eso ; solo que entendiera su humillación. Y es que algo ha cambiado en nuestra forma de vivir la desigualdad. Antes, quien se sabía explotado, podía encontrar fuerza en el colectivo, pero quien hoy se siente despreciado o invisible carga con una herida mucho más solitaria. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La política de la crueldad
items.description: Ya se ha dicho muchas veces: con los resultados del pasado martes comienza el fin de la era Trump . Yo así lo creo y además lo espero, porque esta década de trumpismo no sólo ha destrozado el orden mundial (ese gran cliché) sino que ha degradado a los ciudadanos. A Donald Trump le quedan dos años en los que intentará romper lo que pueda, porque a partir de enero próximo no será solamente lo que en inglés se llama un pato cojo : será un pato cojo resentido, narcisista y sociópata que no tiene ya nada que perder. Luego se irá; y, si los demócratas consiguen recabar un mínimo de sensatez, presentarán un candidato que les permita volver a la Casa Blanca para reparar los destrozos —económicos, políticos, éticos— que Trump deja tras de sí. Pero hay destrozos que no se reparan, o no de inmediato. Trump no solo ha servido de paraguas a los autoritarios y a los plutócratas, no solo ha minado las instituciones con las cuales el mundo intenta ser más vivible, sino que ha normalizado el uso de la crueldad como arma política. Lo que escandalizaba a tantos en 2016 —la burla contra un periodista discapacitado, el menosprecio del sufrimiento de un prisionero de guerra— ya no levanta una ceja. Y ésta es una transformación que no es política, sino moral, y que no se irá a ninguna parte cuando se vaya el nefasto presidente. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Olivos manchados de sangre
items.description: Se dice, se comenta por ahí, que no amas tu ciudad o que la odias, si la criticas. En mi caso particular, llevo criticando Madrid, incluso cuando me gustaba el viejo profesor que la pastoreaba, desde que llegué a su periferia a los doce años. Puede que fuera precisamente esa situación periférica la que me dio una visión privilegiada de las carencias urbanas, porque desde los barrios se percibía todo lo que nos faltaba: metro, parques, servicios sociales. A nadie se le pasaba por la cabeza que salir en manifestación fuera un indicativo de falta de amor. La suerte de Madrid es que siempre ha sido una ciudad criticable. Pero existe hoy un neonacionalismo inspirado por sus dirigentes que trata de acallar las voces de quienes pagando sus impuestos aquí se alzan para decir que no quieren una ciudad destinada solo al beneficio económico, políticas que están esquilmando el carácter de esta querida ciudad imperfecta, a la que “no nos une el amor sino el espanto”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Detenidos por las pintas: decenas de menores en comisaría en Italia con el nuevo arresto preventivo en manifestaciones
items.description: En Italia ya no son ficción las unidades de precrimen, como en la película de Steven Spielberg, Minority Report , en la que el personaje de Tom Cruise veía el futuro y podía actuar antes de que se cometiera un delito. Se trata de arrestos preventivos por lo que la oposición ya llama “delito de sudadera negra”, la prenda más habitual entre los jóvenes que en las últimas semanas han salido a manifestarse en todo el país contra los bajos salarios, el precio de la vivienda y a favor de la paz, la sanidad y la educación públicas. Ya se aplicaba a adultos, pero el último decreto de seguridad de Giorgia Meloni, el octavo, lo ha ampliado a los menores: permite llevar a comisaría antes de una manifestación a quien se considere sospechoso de crear luego altercados en la protesta. El resultado es que el primer día que se puso en práctica, el 24 de octubre, llevó a comisaría a 110 menores en solo 24 horas, aunque según ONG luego ha habido decenas más. Chicos y chicas que han permanecido detenidos durante horas sin haber hecho nada y sin poder llamar a sus padres. Seguir leyendo

items.title: De la nevera al agua del grifo o la luz: los ciberataques ya impactan en la vida cotidiana
items.description: Subir la temperatura de neveras en supermercados de 12 países para estropear toneladas de comida. Dejar colgadas las webs de medio mundo. Ejecutar el mayor robo de la historia . Acceder a datos personales del primer ministro surcoreano y su gabinete. Y al historial médico e información financiera de casi medio millón de moldavos . Este es el resumen de lo que han conseguido los ciberataques más relevantes solo en las últimas dos semanas. Si ampliamos el foco hasta el verano podemos sumar a la lista problemas en la distribución de agua en 12 Estados de EE UU o el hackeo del sistema de salud australiano . Los analistas temen que esta sea la nueva normalidad: un escenario en el que todo, también el mundo físico, se puede tambalear a golpe de teclado y movimiento de ratón. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Motivos y riesgos de una huelga general atípica que pretende marcar “un antes y un después”
items.description: La huelga general del próximo miércoles es, desde múltiples puntos de vista, inédita. Parte de la iniciativa de un movimiento sin capacidad legal para convocarla, el Sindicato de Inquilinas (SDI), y no de los sindicatos de clase tradicionales, UGT y CC OO, que se han sumado a esa reclamación y han sido los que han “legalizado” la convocatoria, explica Valeria Racu, portavoz del SDI. No tiene que ver con cuestiones estrictamente laborales, sino, sobre todo, con las dificultades de acceso a la vivienda. La ministra de Trabajo, Yolanda Díaz, ha animado a la población a participar en ella —“Creo que va a ser la primera vez que no puedo ir de piquete. Bien que me gustaría”, dijo—; el líder de la oposición, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha pedido que se desconvoque —“Las huelgas generales no se convocan contra quien no gobierna”—; y la última fue hace 14 años, en 2012, contra los recortes del Ejecutivo de Mariano Rajoy. items.title: “Parece un Kennedy”: Jon Ossoff, la estrella en ascenso del Partido Demócrata para 2028
items.description: Seis días antes de las elecciones de mitad de mandato en Estados Unidos del pasado martes, el expresidente demócrata Barack Obama saltó al estrado en su último acto de campaña, entre el delirio y los gritos de “yes, we can!” (“¡sí, se puede!”) de las 10.000 personas que atiborraban ese polideportivo de Morrow, al sur de Atlanta (Georgia). Junto a él se encontraba el hombre al que había venido a apoyar, y que recibió otra retumbante ovación. “Solo hay una opción sensata en esta batalla electoral, y ese es Jon Ossoff. No es solamente porque se exprese tan bien; no es solo porque parezca un Kennedy, tan apuesto en los vídeos”, proclamó el primer presidente negro de EE UU. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Esta victoria no basta: ¿qué deben hacer ahora los demócratas?
items.description: Los demócratas no sentían una alegría tan pura desde que Barack Obama fue elegido presidente en 2008 . En cada uno de los Estados en los que Donald Trump ganó con facilidad hace dos años, los candidatos republicanos a cargos públicos de todo tipo han caído derrotados, a menudo por un margen considerable. Los resultados más llamativos son los de Texas , el segundo Estado más poblado del país, en el que los demócratas han conseguido un escaño del Senado de Estados Unidos y el cargo de gobernador, en ambos casos por primera vez desde hacía casi cuatro décadas. El Estado de Kansas, en las grandes llanuras del Medio Oeste, también ha elegido a un demócrata para el Senado, algo que no ocurría desde los años treinta. Seguir leyendo

items.title: De viaje con Kiko Veneno: “Soy pesimista con el mundo, pero mi actitud vital es seguir poniendo rumba”
items.description: Al otro lado del ventanal, el cielo es de un azulado veraniego y una balsa flota despreocupada en un mar en calma de la playa de la Barrosa mientras Kiko Veneno (Figueres, Girona, 74 años) coge la guitarra. En el camerino del Náutico de San Vicente, hay una anarquía propia de una revolución. Entre el ruido de vasos, las conversaciones cruzadas de agosto en vacaciones y los nervios entusiastas de músicos y personal minutos antes de empezar el concierto, los primeros acordes se abren paso mientras los rayos de sol parecen reír en ese pelo blanco platino. Sentado en el sofá, en mitad de la algarabía, Veneno se pone a cantar ‘I’m Only Sleeping’. Con esa voz rumbosa, a medio camino entre el gracejo andaluz y la calle barcelonesa, la canción de The Beatles surge como irreal. Todos van dejando de hablar y, atraídos por la música, buscan candela en la lumbre de la guitarra. Veneno canta, sonríe y mira por la ventana mientras rasga las cuerdas. Ahí, en ese mismo momento, como un trovador que hubiese de ganarse la atención de extraños, cobran sentido las palabras que dijo la noche anterior durante una cena regada de vino blanco y presidida por unos enormes percebes. “Los músicos somos anarquistas subterráneos”, señaló. Sentado a su izquierda, su amigo, el artista plástico Miquel Barceló, asintió con la cabeza y rellenó las copas medio vacías cuando Veneno remató: “Todo nuestro arte no necesita de medallas ni instituciones, sino de encontrarse con la gente corriente y aportarles algo positivo a través de las canciones”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La guerra por la herencia de Brigitte Bardot enfrenta a un marido desheredado y una fundación animalista

Ha ocurrido recientemente, tras la muerte de Alain Delon en agosto de 2024 , que abrió una batalla entre sus tres hijos, aún no resuelta. El caso de Brigitte Bardot, que falleció el 28 de diciembre del año pasado , es más atípico, porque la disputa enfrenta a Bernard d’Ormale, quien fue su pareja durante las últimas tres décadas, y a la Fundación Brigitte Bardot, la que ella misma creó en 1986 para ayudar a los animales y a la que legó su patrimonio. Acompañados de sus padrinos y compañeros, Bürschges y Fanosch quisieron solucionar a sablazos una disputa personal que mantenían abierta. Ambos políticos son Alte Herren , Viejos Caballeros, de la Deutsche Burschenschaft, la organización que reúne a estas hermandades nacionalistas con raíces en el siglo XIX. items.title: Smaller pie, firmer grip
items.description: WHEN railways and factories began transforming 19th-century Europe, the rulers of the Habsburg Empire understood their economic potential. Yet they resisted industrialisation. Friedrich von Gentz, Metternich’s adviser, explained why: “We do not desire at all that the great masses shall become well-off and independent.” His reasoning ended with a revealing question: “How could we otherwise rule over them?” The Habsburg rulers were not necessarily ignorant of the economic benefits of technological progress. They feared its political consequences. A more prosperous society might also become more independent, weakening their grip on power. This historical episode helps explain a persistent puzzle in Pakistan: why do those in power repeatedly choose institutions (rules of the game) and policies that constrain economic progress, even when they too benefit from better alternatives? The answer may lie in the distinction between economic and political returns. Elites do not necessarily choose arrangements that maximise national income, or even their own immediate economic gains. They also consider how a change might affect their ability to retain power and capture future returns — what we call the political replacement effect in economics. Technological and institutional changes can expand economic opportunities while simultaneously creating new centres of political power. Incumbents may, therefore, resist changes that threaten their hold on power. The calculation is straightforward. A reform may make the economy larger and even increase the income of existing elites. But if it also raises the probability of their political displacement, or reduces the share of future gains they can command, their expected returns may decline. Under these conditions, elites may rationally prefer an inferior arrangement that preserves their political dominance. In other words, a smaller pie under a secure scenario may be more attractive than a larger pie with uncertain future distribution. An economically promising change can redistribute political power. Pakistan’s recent history offers three institutional and technological choices that are especially revealing. First is local government. The Constitution requires provinces to devolve political, administrative and financial authority to elected local representatives. Yet successive governments have either delayed local elections or weakened the institutions they create. The largest province, Punjab, last held LG elections a decade ago. Other provinces have also adopted various approaches to limit devolution. KP, for example, recently increased the population threshold for village and neighbourhood councils to reduce the number of councils, potentially weakening representation. In Sindh, transfers to LGs declined from 15.7 per cent of provincial general revenue receipts to just 5.8pc in the 2025-26 budget. What makes these choices economically questionable? Elected LGs with genuine fiscal and administrative authority can better respond to local needs, improve service delivery, and strengthen accountability. Why, then, resist them? Because empowered LGs also create political competitors. A mayor controlling development funds and public services can build an independent political constituency. Legislators lose influence over resources that help sustain their electoral networks. Even if improved local governance generates greater prosperity, its political dividends may accrue to someone else. The second example is fiscal federalism. The seventh NFC award raised provinces’ share of the divisible pool to 57.5pc, with constitutional protection against subsequent reductions. But since then, the federal government has built a parallel fiscal system undermining the very principle of federalism. Petroleum levy collections, which are not shared with provinces, reached Rs1.567 trillion in 2025-26. Provinces were also asked to generate surpluses and, lately, to provide grants to the federal government. The parallel system may be responding to genuine fiscal pressures, but it preserves fiscal discretion at the centre, despite the constitutional commitment to provincial autonomy. In essence, after the seventh NFC, the provincial share fell without anyone touching the award. The political economy consideration here is that meaningful fiscal autonomy changes the distribution of power. Provinces with independent revenue sources and predictable resources can pursue their own priorities and strengthen their political standing. But the provinces are no different. While demanding autonomy from Islamabad, they resist transferring meaningful authority and resources to elected LGs. At each tier, those holding resources resist passing them down. The third example concerns technology: rooftop solar. Faced with high electricity tariffs, the public began investing in their own power generation. Solar offered consumers cheaper electricity, greater reliability, and reduced dependence on the national grid. Yet policy increasingly moved towards discouraging its adoption. The government not only imposed a 10pc sales tax on solar panels but, in February, it replaced net metering with net billing for new connections, substantially lowering the compensation for surplus electricity supplied to the grid. A more economically sustainable response would have restructured costly contractual obligations, modernised the grid, and established fair charges for network use. Why has such adjustment proved so difficult? One explanation is that decentralised electricity generation threatens more than power producers’ revenues. It also weakens an established system through which economic resources, contracts, subsidies, and regulatory discretion are concentrated. These instruments carry financial and political value. Reforming them could improve overall economic performance while reducing the influence of those who currently control them. These three cases are not identical, but they share a key feature: an economically promising change can redistribute political power, creating incentives for incumbents to resist or dilute it. This is what makes the political replacement argument more powerful than the familiar explanation that elites protect their economic rents. Sometimes they may sacrifice economic gains, including their own, to preserve the political position from which future gains can be secured. The implication is that Pakistan’s development problem cannot be resolved through better policy advice alone. The harder challenge is creating institutions that reduce the ability of those in power to obstruct changes that might eventually displace them. The stakes extend beyond the current examples. AI is creating new opportunities while challenging existing economic and political hierarchies. Whether or not Pakistan embraces those opportunities will depend largely on how it responds to a technology most capable of redistributing power. Until the existing calculations change, the country may continue choosing a smaller pie for the sake of a firmer grip. The writer is an associate professor of economics at the Lahore School of Economics. www.waqarwadho.com Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Siblings acquitted in blasphemy case after 20 years
items.description: • SC sets aside death sentences upheld by LHC • Observes findings on mental illness raise doubts about culpability ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Saturday acquitted two brothers in a blasphemy case under Section 295-C of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), setting aside their death sentences earlier upheld by the Lahore High Court (LHC) over a decade ago. A three-judge SC bench, headed by Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi and comprising Justices Shakeel Ahmad and Ishtiaq Ibrahim, took up criminal appeals against the Sept 17, 2015 decision of the LHC. The brothers, Liaqat Ali and Umar Draz, have spent around 20 years behind bars. They were convicted by a sessions judge in Jhang on March 27, 2006. The trial court sentenced both brothers to death and imposed a fine of Rs500,000 each, with five years’ rigorous imprisonment in default. The high court dismissed their appeals and upheld the convictions. The main SC judgement was authored by Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim. Justice Shakeel Ahmad concurred with the order but also annexed an additional note. According to the complaint, Umar Draz had begun making explicit blasphemous statements, leading to a marital dispute between him and his wife that culminated in divorce on March 13, 2006. Draz explicitly affirmed in writing his conversion from Islam in the divorce papers. During the return of his former wife’s dowry articles, a written document auth­ored by co-appellant Liaqat Ali was recovered. It also contained blasphemous assertions. On March 18, 2006, when the complainant and witnesses confronted the brothers over the alleged blasphemous material, both appellants acknowledged and verified the contents of the documents and unequivocally declared their willingness to reiterate their assertions before any forum. Before the SC, their counsel confined his submissions to the plea of mental unsoundness, arguing that the appellants lacked the requisite mens rea (guilty mind) at the time of the alleged offence. The SC examined three psychiatric assessments. An initial three-member medical board at DHQ Hospital, Faisalabad, found both appellants mentally sound in 2007. However, an eight-member Board of Certification diagnosed them with “bipolar affective disorder with psychotic symptoms” in 2023. A nine-member Board of Certification in September 2025 concluded that both brothers were suffering from “bipolar disorder current episode manic”. It described the condition as a chronic illness that was most likely permanent in acute cases, with absent insight and an inability to understand their acts at the time. The SC observed that the unanimous opinions of specialised boards comprising senior professors of psychiatry carried greater weight than the earlier assessm­ent by a board with only one psychiatrist. It also noted that bipolar disorder was episodic and had a genetic component, and that both brothers had been independently diagnosed with the same condition. “The appellants have spent around 20 years behind bars. In the light of the opinion of medical board which raises doubts regarding the culpability of the appellants, the benefit of doubt cannot be withheld from the appellants,” the judgement said. While acquitting the appellants, the SC also expected the executive director of the Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore, to ensure that their medical treatment was not discontinued. Additional note In his concurring note, Justice Ahmad agreed with the acquittal but cautioned that a psychiatric diagnosis alone did not satisfy the requirements of Section 84 of the PPC. The judge distinguished medical insanity from legal insanity, noting that the key question was whether, at the time of the offence, the accused was incapable of knowing the nature of the act or that it was wrong or contrary to law. He argued that legal accountability had to be balanced with humanity, explaining that true justice also included mercy when the law recognised a person’s lack of mental capacity. The note said the medical reports, along with the surrounding circumstances, created reasonable doubt. It also referred to Islamic principles of legal capacity and responsibility. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Trump’s choice
items.description: ALTHOUGH American President Donald Trump has admitted that the disastrous Iran war was a factor in the heavy drubbing his party received from the Democrats in the midterm polls, there are few indications he has decided to wind down the conflict. In fact, Mr Trump has sent mixed messages , saying there has been “progress” in talks with Iran, while also threatening to “destroy what is left” of the Islamic Republic should negotiations fail. These are hardly reassuring words for the international community, which wants the war to end quickly. Qatar has taken centre stage in mediation, with Mr Trump discussing the Iran file with the country’s emir. There is genuine reason to fear another US strike on Iran. For one, Mr Trump may want to act before January 2027, when the new Congress is empowered to scrutinise his decisions. The US government on Saturday asked its citizens in the Middle East to “exercise heightened vigilance”, while it has struck the Iranian island of Qeshm twice this week. The Iranians have not taken the bait, but have promised strong retaliation to new attacks. These developments illustrate the unpredictability of the Gulf situation: one rash move could restart the conflict, which is why mediation efforts should be stepped up. The US leadership is mistaken if it thinks that a fresh round of hostilities would be ‘limited’. If Iran does retaliate to new American or Israeli strikes, the impact of the conflict could be far more devastating than the last round. Along with needless aggression against a sovereign state, the economic shockwave caused by the conflict would hit ordinary people everywhere. In order to prevent a new military and economic crisis, the US leadership must prioritise diplomacy over war. The Iranians want an end to the blockade of their ports, as well as lifting of sanctions and the release of their funds. All these are achievable goals if the US sincerely desires peace. Even the nuclear issue can be resolved at the negotiating table if Mr Trump eschews his threatening tone. In return, Iran should promise unhindered navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Moreover, the ceasefire must be broadened to stop the Yemen conflict as well as Israeli violence in Lebanon and the occupied Palestinian territories. Though technically, these are separate conflicts, they are also interlinked, involving Iran’s allies in the ‘Axis of Resistance’. It is decision time for Mr Trump. He can either work with regional states and negotiate an end to his own ‘forever war’. Or he can continue down the same path, with the international community paying the price for American and Israeli bellicosity. For the sake of peace, it is hoped he chooses the former option. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: U17WWC: You’ve written your names in gold – Tinubu tells Flamingos
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos for making history as the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco. The president, who received the cheering news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States, hailed Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the nation and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. “What wonderful news to return home to! Our young girls have conquered the world and given Nigerians everywhere another reason to celebrate our great country. “To our gallant Flamingos, I say congratulations. You have shown courage, discipline, determination, and the Nigerian spirit of never giving up. “I followed your journey throughout this tournament, and after your semi-final victory, you promised to bring the trophy home. Today, you have kept that promise. You believed in yourselves, fought for one another, and carried our nation’s flag to the very top of the world. “Your victory is an inspiration to millions of young Nigerian girls who dream of achieving greatness. You have shown them that with hard work, opportunity, and determination, they too can reach the highest levels of achievement. “Today, Nigeria celebrates you. You have written your names in gold, and your country is immensely proud of you.” The president particularly applauds Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, whose goals secured the historic victory, while commending the entire squad for their exceptional teamwork throughout the tournament. He also congratulates the coaching crew, the Nigeria Football Federation, and the National Sports Commission for their contributions to the team’s success. President Tinubu reaffirms his administration’s commitment to investing in grassroots sports development and expanding opportunities for young Nigerians, particularly girls, to discover, nurture, and fulfill their potential. “Congratulations once again, Flamingos. Thank you for making Nigeria proud.” The post U17WWC: You’ve written your names in gold – Tinubu tells Flamingos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ruling coalition inches ahead on electoral reforms
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The ruling coalition partners have formally submitted the names of their nominees for the proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, while nominations from opposition parties are still awaited. Talking to Dawn , Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry confirmed that he had received the names from coalition parties, including the PPP. Declining to disclose the names, the minister said the committee would comprise 30 members from the National Assembly and the Senate, with parties receiving representation proportionate to their strength in the two houses of parliament. Under the formula, he said, the PPP would have seven members on the committee, while the PML-N would be allocated 10 seats. However, he added: “The PML-N may have to sacrifice some of its members to accommodate smaller parties.” Opposition yet to submit nominees for parliamentary panel on reforms as PTI doubts govt intent The minister said he had requested the chief whip of the main opposition party, PTI, Aamir Dogar, to provide a list of the party’s nominees for the committee, but Mr Dogar had sought some time. The other opposition party, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), had also not submitted the names of its proposed members, he said. The PTI had objected to the composition of the committee, he said, adding that he had informed the party that all previous parliamentary committees had been constituted on a proportional basis. The minister expressed hope that the PTI would announce its decision next week. Interestingly, Dr Chaudhry said his own party, the ruling PML-N, had shortlisted names for the committee, but these would be submitted to the National Assembly Secretariat only after final approval from the party leadership. Replying to a question, Dr Chaudhry said that if opposition parties decided to boycott the committee, the leadership of the ruling coalition parties would make a final decision on the matter. In a recent post on X, Dr Chaudhry had said that the allocation of seats in the Senate for the committee would give two seats each to the PML-N, PPP and PTI. The Awami National Party (ANP), Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), National Party and JUI-F would each be allocated one seat, he had stated. “The final decision on the names of committee members will be made by the leader of the house [the prime minister] and the deputy prime minister after consultations with the opposition, coalition partners and relevant parliamentary leaders,” Dr Chaudhry said. Earlier this week, the government, taking ownership of an initiative to bring all parliamentary parties, including the opposition, to the negotiating table on electoral reforms, had formally approached its allies to join the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER). PTI serious about reforms When contacted, PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said the party was serious about electoral reforms but had doubts that the government wanted to ensure PTI’s representation on the committee merely to legitimise the process. “The government wants to have five opposition members on the committee. With five members, we will not be able to implement our proposals,” he explained. Replying to a question, Sheikh Waqas said the matter would first have to be discussed in the party’s political committee and then in its parliamentary and core committees. “We held meetings of both committees a few days ago, but due to Imran Khan’s health issues, it was decided to limit their agenda to one point — the health of Imran Khan,” he said. He said the PTI was very clear about its position on electoral reforms and wanted electronic voting machines and a mechanism to ensure that no one could rig elections. “It was the PTI that introduced electronic voting machines and tried them in Pakistan,” he said. Asked how many days the PTI would take to decide whether to become part of the electoral reforms committee, Mr Waqas said meetings of the parliamentary and core committees would be held within two to three days to make a decision. “However, I want to make it clear that the PTI wants electoral reforms and will become part of any sincere effort to ensure that true representatives of the masses run the country,” he said. Talking to Dawn , JUI-F spokesperson Aslam Ghouri said the party had not yet made any decision regarding the PCER. He expressed hope that the matter would soon be discussed by the party’s executive committee. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Ex-AJK president Raja Zulqarnain dies at 93
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Former Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) president Raja Mohammad Zulqarnain Khan died at a hospital in Islamabad on Saturday after a brief illness. He was 93. The AJK government announced a day of official mourning on Sunday, during which the state’s flag would fly at half-mast. It also ordered his burial with full state honours in his native town of Kasguma, Bhimber district, following funeral prayers at 11am on Sunday. Born on March 15, 1933, Raja Zulqarnain was the son of Khan Bahadur Raja Mohammad Afzal Khan, an ICS officerfrom the Chib Rajput tribe who served in Maharaja Hari Singh’s administration. He was granted an estate in present-day Bhimber district. Raja Zulqarnain received his early education in Srinagar and Delhi before joining Lawrence College, Ghora Gali, at the age of 13. His contemporaries there included former prime minister Zafarullah Jamali and former Balochistan chief minister Sardar Akbar Bugti. After graduating from Government College, Lahore, in 1955, he entered the construction business in 1958 by establishing United Builders in Karachi. The company subsequently undertook projects in Pakistan, AJK, UAE and Iraq. Raja Zulqarnain entered politics in 1960-61 as an associate of KH Khurshid, former AJK president and private secretary to Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah. He was elected chairman of his native union council, Kasguma,in the first elections held under the Basic Democracies system introduced by Gen Ayub Khan in Pakistan and subsequently adopted in AJK under Mr Khurshid. When Mr Khurshid founded the Jammu Kashmir Liberation League in 1962, he appointed Raja Zulqarnain its founding secretary general.He remained deeply influenced byhis mentor’s political outlook and personal manner. Ahead of AJK’s first general elections under the parliamentary system in 1975, Raja Zulqarnain joined the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and was elected to the Legislative Assembly from Samahni. Following the restoration of political activities after Gen Ziaul Haq’s martial law, he joined the Muslim Conference (MC) and won the 1985 election from Bhimberon its ticket. He served in Sardar Sikandar Hayat’s cabinet for five years. In 1990, he lost the assembly election to PPP candidate Chaudhry Sohbat Ali. He returned to the assembly in 1991 and served in Sardar Abdul Qayyum Khan’s cabinet for five years. In 1996, the MC secured his election to the AJK Council. In the general elections held that year, he backed Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, who was elected to the assembly for the first time. Their political association, however, ended amid local rivalries ahead of the 2001 election, when Mr Farooq contested as an independent and defeated Raja Zulqarnain. In 2006, Raja Zulqarnain opposed Mr Farooq, the MC nominee, helping Chaudhry Anwarul Haq win his first assembly seat by a narrow margin. In August that year, the Muslim Conference elected him AJK president, a position he held until August 2011. He continued to support Mr Haq in the 2011 and 2016 elections, both of which Mr Farooq won. In 2021, Mr Haq, then a PTI candidate, secured his second victory with Raja Zulqarnain’s support. The former president subsequently became disenchanted with Mr Haq. In April this year, a PML-N delegation called on Raja Zulqarnain and invited him to formally join the party. His son, Babar Ali Zulqarnain, announced his father’s decision to join the PML-Nat a public meeting in Bhimber the following month and was appointed a party vice president. In his condolence message, AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq described Raja Zulqarnain’s death as a major loss for the political, parliamentary and social circles of Jammu and Kashmir. Former AJK premier Sardar Tanveer Ilyas also expressed deep sorrow over Raja Zulqarnain’s death. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Poland in shock after six killed in Krakow mass shooting
items.description: A Polish gunman likely influenced by far-right ideology killed six people in the main square of the southern city of Krakow before police shot and arrested him, officials said on Saturday, adding that three more bodies were found at his home. "Everything points to the fact that the shooter was influenced by far-right ideology, a matter that will also be subject to investigation," Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski told a news briefing. "Police officers are on-site, as are agents from the Internal Security Agency, both here at the scene and at the individual's family home." According to police, the alleged gunman was a 24-year-old Polish citizen. The scenes of blood and bodies strewn across the historic heart of one of Poland's main tourist attractions shocked a nation that has long viewed itself as safer than its western European neighbors, which have witnessed such attacks in the past. The mass shooting, unprecedented in scale, adds to a sense of unease fueled by a series of school stabbings in October, which authorities said were influenced by violent and extremist content online. Polish authorities said four women and two men were killed in the attack in the city center. Seventeen others, including two police officers and the assailant, were wounded. Police said one of the victims identified so far was a British citizen. An Interior Ministry spokesperson said the five foreign nationals injured in the shooting were from Austria, Germany, Portugal, Russia and Britain. A spokesperson for the Lesser Poland Voivodeship office, in the southern region where Krakow is located, told Reuters shortly after midnight local time that the injured police officers were in stable condition after undergoing surgery. The justice minister also called for blood donations for one of the wounded officers. The spokesperson also said the shooter was in "stable but very critical condition" after multiple surgeries. Videos posted online showed the assailant falling to the ground during a close-range shootout with police officers firing handguns. Bodies found at gunman's house Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that the bodies of two women and one man had been found at the shooter's home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, just under 200 kilometers north of Krakow. "There are strong indications that they are members of his immediate family," Tusk told a crisis meeting. He said a drone had been used to look inside the gunman's home due to potential security threats. "We know that a significant amount of weaponry may be inside the house," he said. Local media in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski reported that residents had been evacuated from the building where the gunman lived and that counterterrorism officers had entered the building. Speaking alongside the prime minister, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister coordinating special services, said Poland's Internal Security Agency and Military Counterintelligence Service were supporting the investigation. Military-style clothes Katarzyna Cislo, a local police spokesperson, said: "The shooter was wearing military-like clothes and used military weapons. Many ... weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle too." Police spokesperson Andrzej Fijolek told private broadcaster TVN24 that the assailant used an AR-15 rifle and had a firearms license. "The only known perpetrator of the incident is in police custody," police said in a post on X. They did not mention a motive for the shootings. Police said they began receiving reports at around 3 p.m. (1400 GMT) that an assailant had opened fire from a car and was shooting randomly at people in the square in Poland's second-largest city, a popular tourist destination. Unverified footage shared on social media showed people fleeing the scene as shots rang out and police sirens blared. Other videos showed two people lying on blood-spattered paving stones as bystanders tried to resuscitate them. A third person lay motionless on the ground nearby. "I saw shots being fired from the driver's side window, and smoke was coming out. I ran to the police station in the main market square; when I burst inside, it was full of people hiding on the floor," a man who gave his name only as Konrad and witnessed the shooting told news website Interia. A 67-year-old man named Julek told Reuters that he saw a dark car appear suddenly before the driver started shooting at a group of people and drove off. "If we had been two minutes earlier, we might have been shot," he said. Unverified footage on social media showed the shooting in the Main Market Square as traditional horse-drawn carriages, popular with tourists, passed through or were parked nearby. A man could be seen taking cover in one of the many restaurants and cafes lining the elegant square. National mourning Kierwinski praised the heroism of officers who apprehended the suspect. "The police prevented a much larger massacre that could have otherwise occurred," he said. "They fired shots at the attacker just three minutes after receiving the report." A spokesperson for President Karol Nawrocki said he would declare November 8 and 9 national days of mourning. "My thoughts are with the victims, those injured, and their families," Nawrocki wrote on X. (With input from Reuters)

items.title: PHC removes pleas against emergency, detentions from cause lists
items.description: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court on Saturday removed around 105 petitions from its Nov 10 cause lists, including those challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province as well as the alleged illegal detention of dysfunctional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and several other PTI lawmakers, leaders and workers. The move comes a day after the high court’s administrative committee, acting in compliance with a restraining order issued by the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), decided not to proceed with petitions filed under Article 199 of the Constitution on or after Oct 12. The FCC had also decided not to entertain fresh petitions and to return them to the petitioners, directing them to approach the “appropriate” forum. On Nov 5, a two-member FCC bench declared: “Since the armed forces have been called to act in aid of civil power in the entire province of KP pursuant to the Oct 11 order… the proceedings before the PHC instituted under Article 199 on or after Oct 12 shall, in terms of Clause 4 of Article 245, remain suspended.” Step taken in light of Constitutional Court’s restraining order It also directed KP advocate general Sanaullah Khan to produce within seven days a report, identifying areas in the province where the armed forces are no longer required to act in aid of civil power. The FCC declared that it might consider modifying its order under Article 245 of the Constitution, which provides for the deployment of armed forces in aid of civil power, after examining the report. The FCC order has affected several high-profile cases, as well as routine matters falling under Article 199 of the Constitution. The most significant of the deleted petitions were those challenging the imposition of emergency in KP under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. These petitions were filed by PTI chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan , leaders of Tehreek Tahafuz-i-Aeen Pakistan and the National Democratic Movement, the KP Bar Council and others. During the previous hearing on Oct 20, a two-member bench sought comments on the petitions from the respondents, including the federal government, within a fortnight and fixed Nov 10 for the next hearing. Similarly, petitions challenging the alleged illegal detention or abduction of Sohail Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar, scores of lawmakers, and other PTI leaders and workers were also deleted. In these petitions, the court had initially issued notices on Oct 20 to the KP chief secretary, home secretary, inspector general of police (IGP) and Peshawar Capital City Police Officer, directing them to submit a detailed report within 10 days regarding the whereabouts of the chief minister and clarify whether he had been arrested or was implicated in any criminal case. However, the respondents failed to submit the report within the stipulated time. Consequently, on Nov 3, a bench referred the matter to the chief justice, suggesting the constitution of a larger bench to hear it. Several petitions challenging detentions under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, which had also been fixed for Nov 10, were deleted from the cause list. The deleted petitions also included one filed by KP Assembly Deputy Speaker Suriya Bibi , challenging the government’s sealing of her official residence. In that petition, the court had earlier granted her interim relief, ordering the de-sealing of her residence and allowing her to stay there. However, the government did not comply with the order, prompting the court on Nov 5 to seek an explanation as to why it had not yet been implemented. Similarly, multiple petitions filed by aggrieved property owners against the government’s anti-encroachment operations in different areas were also de-listed. Moreover, several petitions pertaining to “missing persons” and those filed by Afghan nationals seeking relief in the government’s ongoing repatriation drive were also removed from the cause list. The Interior Ministry issued an order on Oct 11 under Article 245 of the Constitution, authorising the deployment of Pakistan Army troops in aid of civil power in KP for the duration of the proclamation issued under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. Meanwhile, the Insaf Lawyers Forum (ILF) has said that no judicial or administrative order should become a means of violating citizens’ fundamental rights and constitutional protections. It termed the “limiting” of the fundamental rights of 45 million people in KP through a court order a serious blow to the supremacy of the Constitution, independence of the judiciary and the right to justice. In a statement, ILF central information secretary Masooma Mir noted that Article 199 of the Constitution provided citizens with a constitutional avenue to approach the high court, while Articles 9, 10-A and 25 guaranteed fundamental rights, including the right to life, fair trial and equality. She added that protecting those rights was the fundamental responsibility of the state and the judiciary. Ms Mir said courts existed to protect citizens’ constitutional rights, not to restrict their access to justice. She urged the Pakistan Bar Council, KP Bar Council, Supreme Court Bar Association and other lawyer bodies to play an active role in the current constitutional crisis to safeguard the rights of the people of the province. Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

items.title: Guinée : Un élève coranique tente de poignardé un imam lors de la prière du vendredi
items.description: Un incident survenu à la mosquée de Yeradè, dans le quartier Tata 2, a suscité l’émoi parmi les fidèles. Le jeune homme a été maîtrisé par des fidèles avant que la situation ne dégénère. Un incident inhabituel s’est produit ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026 à la mosquée de Yeradè, située dans le quartier Tata 2, au centre-ville de Labé, en Guinée. Un jeune disciple coranique s’est introduit dans l’édifice religieux avec un couteau, alors que la prière du jour tirait à sa fin. Selon des informations rapportées par Africaguinee, le jeune homme a accédé à la mosquée par son côté Est, avant de traverser les rangs des fidèles en direction de la porte réservée aux imams. Son comportement a rapidement suscité l’inquiétude des personnes présentes. Il a finalement été stoppé à l’intérieur de la mosquée grâce à l’intervention d’un muezzin et d’autres disciples coraniques. La prière a pu s’achever normalement. Le couteau lui a ensuite été retiré et le jeune homme a été reconduit à son domicile. Un comportement inhabituel signalé la veille D’après des témoignages recueillis auprès d’habitants du secteur et de certains talibés, le jeune homme présenterait des troubles de santé mentale et communiquerait très peu ces derniers temps. Ces déclarations n’ont toutefois pas été confirmées par un avis médical. Les mêmes témoins indiquent qu’il s’était déjà présenté à la mosquée à trois reprises le jeudi précédent, aux heures de prière, avec le souhait de diriger l’office religieux. Il est revenu le vendredi, cette fois avec un couteau. Des agents de sécurité se sont rendus sur les lieux après l’incident. Toutefois, après avoir constaté l’état du jeune homme, ils seraient repartis sans l’emmener, selon les témoins cités par Africaguinee. L’article Guinée : Un élève coranique tente de poignardé un imam lors de la prière du vendredi est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: 11 décembre au Burkina Faso : Retour du défilé militaire après 6 ans d’interruption
items.description: À l’occasion de la montée des couleurs de la garnison de Ouagadougou, le vendredi 6 novembre 2026, le ministre d’État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le Général de division Célestin Simporé, a présenté le bilan des activités d’octobre et dévoilé plusieurs orientations stratégiques. Parmi les annonces majeures figurent les 96 000 inscriptions à la réserve militaire et la reprise du grand défilé militaire du 11-Décembre. La Base aérienne 511 de Ouagadougou a accueilli, le vendredi 6 novembre 2026, la cérémonie de montée des couleurs de la garnison de Ouagadougou. Présidée par le Général de division Célestin Simporé, ministre d’État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, cette cérémonie a été l’occasion de faire le point sur les principales activités du département et de communiquer les nouvelles orientations aux troupes et au commandemet militaire. Au titre du bilan institutionnel, le ministère s’est classé deuxième à l’exposition gouvernementale organisée dans le cadre de la deuxième phase de la troisième édition des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne. Revenant sur la commémoration du 15 octobre, le ministre a rappelé le message du président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, relatif à la nécessité de renforcer l’unité nationale face aux menaces extérieures. Réserve militaire : plus de 96 000 inscrits sur 100 000 attendus L’un des principaux points abordés concerne la campagne de recrutement de la réserve militaire. Selon le Général Célestin Simporé, le processus a déjà enregistré plus de 96 000 inscriptions, sur un objectif de 100 000 hommes et femmes. Cette mobilisation vise à renforcer les capacités nationales de défense et à consolider la souveraineté du Burkina Faso. Sur le volet de la discipline militaire, le ministre a également annoncé qu’une grâce présidentielle avait été accordée à neuf militaires par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, à l’issue d’une évaluation rigoureuse. Il a rappelé que la discipline demeure un fondement essentiel de l’organisation et de l’efficacité des forces armées. Opérations militaires : des bases terroristes détruites dans la Boucle du Mouhoun Abordant la situation sécuritaire, le ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique a assuré que les forces combattantes maintenaient l’ascendant sur les groupes armés terroristes. Il a notamment fait état de la destruction de bases terroristes, particulièrement dans la région de la Boucle du Mouhoun. Sur le plan diplomatique, le Burkina Faso a également marqué sa présence au sommet Afrique-Russie à Moscou, dans le cadre de la diversification de ses partenariats internationaux. Le Général Simporé a par ailleurs évoqué le succès du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) et l’organisation du Tour du Faso comme des illustrations du dynamisme du pays. Le grand défilé militaire du 11-Décembre fait son retour Autre annonce importante de cette cérémonie : la reprise du grand défilé militaire du 11-Décembre, après six années d’interruption. Cette décision marque le retour d’un rendez-vous majeur des célébrations de la fête nationale, qui met traditionnellement en valeur les forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi que les capacités des institutions militaires. Pour conclure son intervention, le ministre a félicité les personnels militaires et civils décorés pour leur engagement et leur contribution au service de la Nation. À travers cette cérémonie, le ministère entend ainsi réaffirmer ses priorités autour de la discipline, de la mobilisation patriotique, du renforcement des capacités militaires et de la défense de l’intégrité territoriale. L’article 11 décembre au Burkina Faso : Retour du défilé militaire après 6 ans d'interruption est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Appel à expulser les guinéenns du Burkina : Les guinéens sont chez eux au Burkina rassure le ministre de la Solidarité
items.description: Face aux appels à la vengeance visant la communauté guinéenne après les récents événements, la ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité appelle à l’apaisement. Elle assure que les ressortissants guinéens vivant au Burkina Faso ne doivent faire l’objet d’aucune intimidation ni représaille. La ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, Pélagie Kaboré, a lancé un appel au calme et à la retenue face aux messages de représailles visant les ressortissants guinéens vivant au Burkina Faso. Ces réactions font suite aux récents événements ayant suscité des tensions entre des citoyens des deux pays. Dans une déclaration, la ministre a tenu à rassurer la communauté guinéenne sur sa sécurité et sa place au sein de la société burkinabè. Elle a notamment insisté sur le fait qu’aucun ressortissant guinéen ne devrait être inquiété en raison de cette situation. « Les Guinéens sont ici au Burkina Faso chez eux, et il n’est pas question qu’un Guinéen soit inquiété par la situation qui vient de se passer », a-t-elle affirmé. Le gouvernement rejette les appels à la représaille La camarade Pélagie Kaboré a également précisé que le gouvernement burkinabè n’était associé, ni de près ni de loin, aux appels à la vengeance qui circulent. Elle a dénoncé des comportements qu’elle juge incompatibles avec les valeurs de solidarité africaine et de panafricanisme défendues par le Burkina Faso. « Nous restons profondément africains, profondément panafricanistes, et toutes les communautés sont les bienvenues au Burkina Faso », a-t-elle souligné. À travers cette sortie, la ministre entend prévenir toute stigmatisation des ressortissants guinéens et éviter que les tensions liées aux récents événements ne se transforment en actes de violence contre des personnes étrangères. Son message se veut ainsi un appel à la responsabilité collective, à la coexistence pacifique et au respect de toutes les communautés vivant sur le territoire burkinabè. L’article Appel à expulser les guinéenns du Burkina : Les guinéens sont chez eux au Burkina rassure le ministre de la Solidarité est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Pour avoir insulté un policier lors d’un contrôle routier, Eugène condamné à six mois de prison avec sursis
items.description: Poursuivi pour outrage à agent public après un contrôle routier lié au non-port du casque, Eugène a été reconnu coupable par le tribunal. Le parquet avait requis deux mois de prison ferme, mais la juridiction a finalement prononcé six mois avec sursis et une amende ferme de 250 000 FCFA. Un contrôle routier qui tourne au contentieux judiciaire. Eugène a été condamné à six mois d’emprisonnement avec sursis et à une amende ferme de 250 000 FCFA pour outrage à agent public. La décision a été rendue par le tribunal correctionnel, après examen des faits et audition des différentes parties. À la barre, le policier ayant procédé à son interpellation a confirmé les circonstances rapportées. Selon ses déclarations, le conducteur l’aurait insulté avant d’annoncer qu’il allait récupérer son casque. Interrogé par le président du tribunal sur la véracité de ces faits, le policier a répondu par l’affirmative. Invité à réagir aux déclarations de l’agent, Eugène a reconnu les avoir entendues, tout en contestant les faits dans un premier temps. Il a toutefois exprimé ses regrets et demandé pardon au tribunal. Le parquet réclamait deux mois de prison ferme Dans ses réquisitions, le ministère public a estimé que les faits d’outrage à agent public étaient établis. Il a notamment relevé que le prévenu avait été interpellé à la suite d’un contrôle portant sur le non-port du casque et qu’il avait reconnu les faits depuis son passage au commissariat jusqu’à l’audience. Pour le parquet, les circonstances du contrôle routier ne pouvaient en aucun cas justifier les insultes adressées à l’agent. En conséquence, le ministère public a demandé au tribunal de déclarer Eugène coupable et a requis deux mois d’emprisonnement ferme ainsi qu’une amende de 250 000 FCFA, également ferme. Le tribunal prononce six mois avec sursis Après avoir entendu les différentes parties et examiné le dossier, le tribunal a déclaré Eugène coupable d’outrage à agent public. La juridiction l’a condamné à six mois d’emprisonnement assortis du sursis à exécution et à une amende ferme de 250 000 FCFA. La peine d’emprisonnement prononcée est donc assortie du sursis, contrairement aux réquisitions du parquet qui réclamait une peine ferme. Cette affaire rappelle les conséquences judiciaires que peuvent entraîner les injures et les comportements outrageants envers un agent public dans l’exercice de ses fonctions, y compris lors d’un contrôle routier. L’article Burkina Faso : Pour avoir insulté un policier lors d’un contrôle routier, Eugène condamné à six mois de prison avec sursis est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Cameroun : Une femme enceinte surprise en plein cambriolage
items.description: Accusée d'avoir tenté de dérober une bouteille de gaz, une femme enceinte a été appréhendée par des habitants du quartier PK12, à Douala-Bassa. Elle affirme avoir basculé dans le vol après l'abandon de son compagnon. Une femme enceinte a été interpellée par des habitants de la zone PK12, dans le secteur de Douala-Bassa, au Cameroun, après avoir été soupçonnée de tentative de cambriolage dans une habitation. Selon les informations rapportées, elle aurait été surprise alors qu'elle tentait de dérober une bouteille de gaz. Lors de son interpellation, plusieurs objets compromettants auraient été retrouvés en sa possession, notamment des doubles de clés de plusieurs domiciles, des tournevis et des pinces. Ces outils seraient, selon les témoignages rapportés, utilisés pour faciliter ses opérations. Dans une vidéo largement relayée sur les réseaux sociaux, la mise en cause donne sa version des faits. Elle explique s'être tournée vers cette activité après avoir été abandonnée par le père de l'enfant qu'elle porte. Après son interpellation par les riverains, la femme a été remise aux éléments de la gendarmerie pour la suite de la procédure. L’article Cameroun : Une femme enceinte surprise en plein cambriolage est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: États-Unis : L’avocat de l’accusé du meurtre de Tupac Shakur, retrouvé mort
items.description: L’avocat américain Michael Sanft, âgé de 55 ans, qui avait assuré gratuitement la défense de Duane Davis dans l’affaire du meurtre du rappeur Tupac Shakur, a été retrouvé mort à Las Vegas. Les circonstances de son décès restent inconnues. Michael Sanft, avocat de 54 ans, a été retrouvé mort à Las Vegas, aux États-Unis. Il s'était fait connaître pour avoir assuré gratuitement la défense de Duane Davis, poursuivi dans le cadre de l'assassinat du célèbre rappeur américain Tupac Shakur. Selon les informations rapportées par le Las Vegas Review-Journal, son corps a été découvert à son domicile dans la matinée du vendredi 6 novembre 2026. Un proche a confirmé son décès. Le bureau du médecin légiste du comté de Clark a indiqué que les causes et les circonstances de sa mort n'étaient pas encore déterminées. La police a toutefois précisé que le décès ne semblait pas suspect. Pour rappel, Duane « Keffe D » Davis a été reconnu coupable en août 2026 pour son rôle dans l'assassinat de Tupac Shakur, tué par balles à Las Vegas en septembre 1996. Le 13 octobre 2026, il a été condamné à 40 ans de prison minimum. Quelques jours avant son décès, Michael Sanft avait déposé un recours en appel contre la condamnation de son client, le 30 octobre 2026. L’article États-Unis : L'avocat de l’accusé du meurtre de Tupac Shakur, retrouvé mort est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Côte d’Ivoire : Une dispute autour de 650 F CFA vire au meurtre à Assalé Kouassikro
items.description: Un différend portant sur la somme de 650 F CFA a coûté la vie à un jeune homme dans le village d’Assalé Kouassikro, situé dans la sous-préfecture de Kregbé, dans la région d’Arrah. Le présumé auteur a été maîtrisé par des habitants puis remis à la gendarmerie. Un jeune homme a perdu la vie après avoir été poignardé lors d'une altercation à Assalé Kouassikro, un village relevant de la sous-préfecture de Kregbé, dans la région d’Arrah, en Côte d’Ivoire. À l’origine du drame, une dispute autour d’une somme de 650 francs CFA qui aurait dégénéré jusqu’à une issue mortelle. Au cours de l’altercation, l’un des protagonistes aurait porté un coup de couteau à son adversaire, qui n’a pas survécu à ses blessures. Face à la gravité des faits, des habitants du village sont rapidement intervenus. Ils ont réussi à maîtriser le présumé auteur avant de le remettre aux éléments de la gendarmerie. Une enquête devrait permettre de déterminer les circonstances exactes de cette affaire et d’établir les responsabilités. Un différend portant sur quelques centaines de francs CFA qui se termine par la perte d’une vie que s'est dommage ! items.title: Burkina Faso : La Faso FDA suspend la fabrication et la vente des produits « Cyclone » après la découverte de sildénafil
items.description: Des analyses de laboratoire ont révélé la présence de sildénafil, une substance médicamenteuse utilisée contre les troubles de l’érection, dans quatre produits de la gamme « Cyclone » commercialisés par YELEMANY BAA SARL à Bobo-Dioulasso. La Faso FDA appelle les consommateurs à cesser immédiatement leur utilisation. La Faso Food and Drug Administration (Faso FDA) tire la sonnette d’alarme sur la commercialisation de plusieurs produits de la gamme « Cyclone » au Burkina Faso. Dans un communiqué, l’institution annonce que des analyses de laboratoire ont mis en évidence la présence de sildénafil dans des échantillons de ces produits fabriqués et commercialisés par la société YELEMANY BAA SARL, basée à Bobo-Dioulasso. La substance détectée, le sildénafil, est un médicament utilisé dans le traitement des troubles de l’érection. Son utilisation nécessite un encadrement médical en raison des risques qu’elle peut présenter, notamment chez les personnes souffrant de maladies cardiovasculaires ou d’hypertension, les personnes âgées ainsi que celles prenant des médicaments à base de dérivés nitrés. Le problème, selon la Faso FDA, est que cette substance n'est pas mentionnée sur l’étiquetage des produits concernés, pourtant présentés comme des boissons ou des compléments alimentaires « 100 % naturels ». Quatre produits concernés par l’alerte sanitaire L’alerte porte sur l’ensemble des produits de la gamme « Cyclone », quels que soient leurs numéros de lot et leurs lieux d’achat. Il s’agit notamment de : – Cyclone Classique ; – Cyclone Retard ; – Cyclone Sirop ; – Cyclone Poudre. Face à cette situation, la Faso FDA demande aux consommateurs de ne plus acheter ni consommer ces produits. Les personnes qui en détiennent encore sont invitées à interrompre immédiatement leur utilisation. L’institution recommande également aux personnes ayant consommé ces produits et présentant des symptômes tels que des douleurs thoraciques, des malaises, des vertiges importants, une baisse brutale de la vue ou de l’audition, ou encore une érection douloureuse durant plus de quatre heures, de se rendre sans délai dans un centre de santé en signalant le produit consommé. Fabrication et commercialisation suspendues Au-delà de l’appel à la vigilance, la Faso FDA annonce la suspension, à titre conservatoire, de la fabrication et de la vente de tous les produits de la gamme « Cyclone ». Les grossistes, commerçants, boutiques, kiosques et vendeurs en ligne sont sommés de retirer immédiatement ces produits de leurs stocks et points de vente, de les mettre en quarantaine et de se conformer aux instructions des équipes d’inspection chargées de leur récupération. À travers cette alerte, la Faso FDA invite par ailleurs les populations à faire preuve de prudence face aux produits qui promettent des effets sur la vigueur sexuelle, la perte de poids ou la guérison de certaines maladies. Pour tout renseignement ou signalement d’un effet indésirable, les consommateurs peuvent contacter la Faso FDA au numéro vert 3535, par WhatsApp au 52 25 30 30, ou consulter ses plateformes officielles. L’article Burkina Faso : La Faso FDA suspend la fabrication et la vente des produits « Cyclone » après la découverte de sildénafil est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .
